title: Alerts & notifications
body:
## Context
Alerts are the notification half of the rule engine. The plan deliberately gives alerts **no action block**: `AlertConditionIr` (`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`) is the condition half of the rule IR with `actions` omitted, so *an alert can never place an order regardless of what the user authors*. That single decision is what lets alerts be authored casually, evaluated cheaply and delivered to many channels without dragging the OMS safety invariants along.

E40 delivers module **M22** (alert evaluator + delivery dispatcher) on top of E35's IR, compiler, metric vocabulary and evaluator, and surfaces it through four screens and the shell notification furniture that E10 mounted empty. Alerts are evaluated **server-side** so they fire with the client closed (US-ALRT-001 NFR), delivered through the transactional `outbox` so a crash between "decide" and "send" can neither lose nor duplicate a notification (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.10.4), and every firing is recorded in the append-only `alert_deliveries` table with the evaluation snapshot attached, because *no channel may be the single source of truth* (US-ALRT-005 NFR).

Roadmap placement: `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 — 21 points, S18–S19, train R3, after E35 lands the IR (`E35 --> E40` in the §11.1 dependency graph).

> **Sizing note (roadmap alignment).** `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 allocates E40 **21 points, S18–S19**. This backlog is sized to that allocation: the design, engineering, QA and security work previously split across 25 child tickets is consolidated into 15, so the epic total and the sum of its children are both 21 and the engineering subtotal (Story + Task + Spike) is 20, inside the ±15% band (17.85–24.15). No scope was dropped — every deliverable, acceptance scenario and sign-off gate from the superseded tickets is carried verbatim in the merged bodies, under a labelled *Part A/B/C* heading naming its origin.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Stories (US)**: US-ALRT-001 price alerts, US-ALRT-002 indicator/metric alerts, US-ALRT-003 order-flow & detector alerts, US-ALRT-004 alert centre, US-ALRT-005 delivery channels, US-ALRT-006 snooze/mute/quiet hours, US-ALRT-008 webhook delivery (Could — descoped to R5 per §12 descoping ladder row 6).
- **Backend (M22)**: `apps/api/cv/alerts/` — alert repository, condition compiler (notify-only IR subset), evaluator subscribing to the E35 metric bus, cooldown/trigger-mode/snooze/expiry gating, storm suppression, delivery dispatcher over `outbox`.
- **DB**: migration `0009_alerts` — `alerts`, `alert_deliveries` (append-only), plus the `alert.deliver` and `webhook.post` outbox topics.
- **REST**: `GET/POST /api/v1/alerts`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}`, `PUT /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}/enabled`, `GET /api/v1/alerts/deliveries`, `POST /api/v1/alerts/deliveries/{deliveryId}/ack`, `POST /api/v1/alerts/deliveries/ack-all`, `GET /api/v1/notifications`.
- **WS**: topic `alerts` (`AlertUpdate`, options `unacked_only`, cadence 250 ms, permission `alerts:read`, own alerts only).
- **Screens**: SCR-090 Alerts centre, SCR-091 Alert editor, SCR-092 Alert triggered toast/detail, SCR-014 Notification centre *content*, SCR-115 Notifications settings, SCR-015 toast variants for fired alerts.
- **Components**: CMP-163 AlertRow, CMP-164 AlertBuilderForm, CMP-165 AlertFiredToastGroup (new/extended), composed with CMP-045, CMP-049, CMP-055, CMP-060, CMP-209, CMP-212.
- **Design**: E40-D01..D06. **QA**: E40-Q01..Q05. **Security**: E40-X01..X03.

## Out of scope
- **US-ALRT-007 alert-to-action automation (Could)** — deliberately not built here. Binding an action to a signal is a *rule*, authored in E35/E36/E37 with the full arming, step-up and risk path; E40 keeps the "alerts cannot act" invariant absolute.
- Rule IR, compiler, metric vocabulary service and evaluator — E35.
- The shell chrome that hosts notifications (CMP-209 RightRail, CMP-212 ToastHost mount) — E10 built them; E40 fills them with content.
- Email transport infrastructure (SMTP relay provisioning) — E04 infra; E40 consumes the configured relay.
- Push notifications to mobile — Android is out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14.
- Prometheus/Alertmanager operational alerting (E04-T05) — a different kind of "alert"; E40 is user-facing only.

## Acceptance criteria

*(epic level)*
```gherkin
Scenario: Alerts fire with no client connected
  Given a price alert on BTCUSDT and every browser and Electron window closed
  When the condition is met
  Then the firing is recorded in alert_deliveries within 1 s of the condition being met
  And on next connect the alert centre and the notification centre both show it unacked
Scenario: An alert can never place an order
  When a corpus of hand-crafted payloads attempts to smuggle an action node into condition_ir via POST /api/v1/alerts
  Then every payload is rejected 422 with RuleIrInvalid and no OMS call is made
Scenario: Storm suppression keeps the UI usable
  Given more than 20 alerts would fire for one user in one minute
  Then they aggregate into a summary delivery, the suppression is visible in the alert centre, and no individual firing is lost from history
Scenario: Critical notifications survive muting
  Given quiet hours are on, ETHUSDT is muted and every optional channel is off
  When a risk lockout, kill-switch or connection-loss notification is raised
  Then it is still delivered, and the attempt to mute a risk channel is audited as notifications.risk_channel_muted
```

## Technical notes / design
Module **M22 AlertService** decomposes into three collaborators:
1. `AlertCompiler` — wraps E35's IR validator, additionally asserting the payload matches `AlertConditionIr` (no `actions` key, no action-bearing operand) and that every referenced metric exists in the E35 registry.
2. `AlertEvaluator` — one subscription per *distinct compiled condition hash* (`alerts.condition_hash`), fanned out to the alert rows sharing it, so N alerts on `last_price` cost one metric subscription. Gating order on every candidate fire: `enabled` → `deleted_at IS NULL` → `expires_at` → `snoozed_until` → `trigger_mode` → `cooldown_seconds` → storm suppressor → dispatch.
3. `DeliveryDispatcher` — writes one `alert_deliveries` row plus one `outbox` row per channel inside the firing transaction; a poller delivers and advances `queued → sent | failed | suppressed`, `acked` on user ack.

Trigger modes (`alert_trigger_mode`): `once` (fire then set `enabled=false`), `every_time` (subject to `cooldown_seconds`), `once_per_bar` (keyed on the trigger's `timeframe` bar open). Alerts **never expire on a timer** unless `expires_at` is explicitly set (US-ALRT-001 scenario 3).

## Test plan
Layer coverage is specified per child ticket. Epic-level gates: contract tests on every `/alerts*` operation and the `alerts` WS topic; an integration suite replaying a recorded Bybit window and asserting the exact firing sequence; a k6 profile at 500 armed alerts × 50 msg/s; the storm and chaos scenarios in E40-Q02; the a11y audit in E40-Q02.

## Security notes
STRIDE in E40-X01. Headline threats: **SSRF via webhook URL** (an owner-supplied URL that targets the loopback/metadata/Tailscale control plane), **secret leakage into a notification body** (message templates interpolate the rule context — the interpolator must be allow-listed), **tampering with history** (`alert_deliveries` is append-only with a `forbid_mutation` DELETE trigger), **notification-channel muting as an attack** (muting risk alerts is audited at high severity), and **information disclosure across users** (`alerts:read` is `scope: self`). `alerts.webhook_url_enc` and `alerts.webhook_secret_enc` are SECRET-classified columns and are never returned by any API.

## Accessibility notes
Four UI surfaces, all WCAG 2.2 AA. Alert lists are real tables with status as text; the fired toast is `role="status"` (never assertive — it must not interrupt order entry); sound is never the only channel; the notification settings matrix uses row+column headers; auto-dismissing toasts always have a persistent backstop in SCR-014 (WCAG 2.2.1).

## Performance notes
Budget set: condition met → visible toast ≤2 s end to end (SCR-092), in-app record ≤1 s (US-ALRT-001 NFR); alert-centre list cursor-paginated and live-updated at ≤1 Hz (SCR-090); `alerts` WS cadence 250 ms; notification centre renders 500 rows with ≤8 ms scripting per scroll frame (SCR-014); notification sound assets ≤200 KB preloaded (SCR-115); condition validation round-trip ≤300 ms (SCR-091).

## Observability
Metrics `cv_alerts_armed`, `cv_alert_fires_total{trigger_mode}`, `cv_alert_suppressed_total{reason}`, `cv_alert_delivery_total{channel,status}`, `cv_alert_delivery_latency_seconds{channel}`, `cv_alert_eval_latency_seconds`, `cv_outbox_depth{topic}`. Audit events `alerts.create`, `alert.updated`, `alert.enabled_changed`, `alert.deleted`, `notifications.risk_channel_muted`.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2: all children Done or explicitly descoped; epic AC verified end to end; coverage ≥85% on `cv.alerts`, ≥80% frontend; docs 14/15/21/22/23/24 reconciled; axe-core green plus a manual screen-reader pass on all four surfaces; perf numbers recorded against the budgets above; STRIDE findings closed; epic regression pass recorded; demoed to the Owner on staging (demo); retro notes filed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E35` — the IR, the metric vocabulary registry and the evaluator are E35's; E40 adds no new expression grammar. `E25` supplies the detector metrics that US-ALRT-003 alerts on. `E10` supplies the shell mounts (CMP-209, CMP-212). `E39` raises the critical risk notifications whose override behaviour E40 must honour. `E09` supplies `alerts:read`/`alerts:write` and the session scope.

## Branch
`feat/e40-alerts-*` per child ticket; PRs ≤400 LOC diff.

## References

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-014, SCR-015, SCR-090, SCR-091, SCR-092, SCR-115
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-045, CMP-060, CMP-163, CMP-164, CMP-165, CMP-209, CMP-212
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.24
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.5 `alerts` / `alert_deliveries`, §3.10.4 `outbox`
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/alerts`, `/alerts/{alertId}`, `/alerts/{alertId}/enabled`, `/alerts/deliveries`, `/notifications`
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.7 `AlertUpdate`, topic `alerts`
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11 rule IR / metric registry, §12 RBAC permission list
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 E40, §7.3 exit criteria

## Child dependency graph
```mermaid
graph TD
    D01[D01 UX research + a11y design review] --> D02[D02 Hi-fi all five surfaces + DS/motion + handoff pack]
    K01[K01 Spike: evaluation placement & storm thresholds] --> T02[T02 Compiler + alert CRUD API]
    T01[T01 Migration 0009_alerts + repos + outbox topics] --> T02
    T02 --> T03[T03 Evaluator + gating + storm suppression]
    T03 --> T04[T04 Delivery dispatcher + deliveries API + WS alerts]
    D02 --> S01[S01 SCR-090 alerts centre + SCR-091 alert editor]
    T02 --> S01
    T04 --> S01
    D02 --> S02[S02 Toasts, SCR-092 detail, SCR-014 centre content, SCR-115 preferences]
    T04 --> S02
    S01 --> S02
    T04 --> S03[S03 Webhook delivery - deferred to R5]
    X01[X01 STRIDE + abuse cases + security sign-off] --> S03
    T04 --> X01
    S01 --> T05[T05 Docs & ADR reconcile]
    S01 --> Q01[Q01 Test plan, fixtures, E2E + contract automation]
    S02 --> Q01
    Q01 --> Q02[Q02 Perf/storm/chaos + a11y audit + regression pack + QA sign-off]
    S02 --> Q02
    Q02 --> X01
    S02 --> D03[D03 Design QA of the shipped surfaces]
```

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric or alphabetic order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: Research alert attention behaviour and run the a11y design review
body:
## Context
This ticket merges the former E40-D01 (UX research) and E40-D01 (accessibility design review) into one design-discovery ticket, sized against the 21-point roadmap allocation for E40. Part A runs before wireframing and decides the critical-override list; Part B gates the handoff pack produced in E40-D02.

### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
The failure mode of an alerting system is not "it didn't fire" — it is "it fired so often the trader stopped reading it". US-ALRT-003's storm-suppression scenario and US-ALRT-006's mute/quiet-hours story are both reactions to that. Before any pixel is drawn we need evidence on: which events the owner and the account managers actually want interrupted for, which they want logged only, how they expect a one-shot alert to behave after it fires, and what "critical, cannot be muted" should contain.

This research also decides the **critical-override list** (US-ALRT-006 scenario 3) whose contents must be "explicit, documented and covered by tests" per the story's NFR — that list is a product decision, not an engineering one, and this ticket is where it is made.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
Notifications are the single most common place a product breaks WCAG 2.2.1 (no timing-based loss of information) and 4.1.3 (status messages). E40 ships an auto-dismissing toast, a live-updating stream, a sound channel and a preference matrix — four classic traps. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 makes a11y default-on for every UI surface, and `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` is the bar. This review happens *before* handoff so defects are corrected in Figma, not in React.

## Scope / Deliverables
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
- 4–6 moderated sessions (owner + the account-manager personas in `docs/plan/10-personas.md`) with a concept probe covering: a price alert firing, a detector alert firing, a storm of 25 firings, a muted symbol, quiet hours, and a risk lockout arriving during quiet hours.
- Competitive teardown of alerting in TradingView, Bookmap and Sierra Chart: firing modes, notification surfaces, snooze affordances, history retention.
- **Deliverable 1** — `docs/design/research/e40-alert-attention.md`: findings, verbatim quotes, and an interruption taxonomy mapping each notification kind (alert / rule fire / order reject / risk / system / recorder) to a recommended default channel set.
- **Deliverable 2** — the ratified **critical-override list** (candidate set from US-ALRT-006: daily-loss breach, liquidation proximity, connection loss; plus kill-switch engagement and fan-out partial failure from E34/E39) with a written rationale per entry, handed to E40-S02 and E40-Q01 as a test oracle.
- **Deliverable 3** — the storm-suppression product rule: threshold, aggregation window, and the wording of the summary notification, feeding E40-K01 and E40-T03.
- Reviewed and signed off by the Chief Design Officer and the Owner.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
- Written review of SCR-090, SCR-091, SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, producing `docs/design/a11y/e40-alerts-a11y-review.md`.
- **Live-region strategy** ratified and documented per surface: SCR-092 toast `role="status"`; SCR-014 `aria-live="polite"` escalating to `assertive` only for order rejects and risk lockouts; error/rejection toasts routed to CMP-212's separate `role="alert"` region so a critical rejection is never queued behind alert chatter.
- **Timing audit**: every auto-dismissing element paired with a persistent record in SCR-014; pause-on-hover/focus confirmed; no information exists only for a bounded time.
- **Keyboard maps**: full keyboard route for each surface — open centre, move through items, action an item, mark-all-read, snooze, dismiss, escape; the SCR-115 matrix navigable by row and column; the sound preview reachable.
- **Announcement throttling**: a documented rule for a burst of firings (announce the summary, not each item) so a screen reader is not flooded — the a11y counterpart of storm suppression.
- **Non-colour encoding** check: severity, status, snoozed, disabled, delivery-failed all encoded by icon + text.
- Contrast verification of every state in dark, light and high-contrast themes; focus-visible rings on every interactive element at ≥3:1.
- Defects logged back onto E40-D02/E40-D02 and fixed before those tickets close.

## Out of scope
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
Any hi-fi or wireframe pixels (E40-D02/D03). Sound design asset selection (E40-D02). Prometheus/Alertmanager operational alerting (E04).
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
The built-implementation audit (E40-Q02). Non-alert shell chrome (E10).

## Acceptance criteria
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
```gherkin
Scenario: Findings are evidence-backed
  Given the research report is submitted for sign-off
  Then every recommendation cites at least two participant observations or a competitive precedent
  And each is tagged with the US-ALRT id it informs
Scenario: The critical-override list is decision-ready
  Then the list names each overriding notification kind, its source module, and why muting it is unsafe
  And the Owner has explicitly accepted it in the ticket
Scenario: A contested default is escalated, not silently chosen (edge)
  Given participants split on whether desktop notifications default on
  Then both options are written up with consequences and the Owner makes the call on the ticket rather than the designer picking silently
Scenario: Storm threshold is specified numerically (failure guard)
  Then the report states a concrete threshold and window (e.g. ">20 deliveries per user per 60 s") rather than an adjective, so E40-T03 can implement it without interpretation
```
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
```gherkin
Scenario: Every surface has a documented live-region decision
  Then the review states, per surface, the region role, its politeness, what is announced and what is deliberately not
Scenario: No information is lost to timing
  Given any auto-dismissing toast
  Then the review demonstrates the same content is retrievable from SCR-014 afterwards, satisfying WCAG 2.2.1
Scenario: A firing storm does not flood the screen reader (edge)
  Given 25 alerts fire in one minute
  Then the documented announcement rule produces one summary announcement, and the individual items remain readable on demand
Scenario: Defects block handoff (failure)
  Given a review defect of severity major
  Then E40-D02 cannot start until it is fixed in the design file and re-verified
```

## Technical notes / design
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
Sessions run against the E26 replay harness on staging (demo) so participants see real recorded bursts rather than mock data — a synthetic storm is not credible enough to elicit real preferences. Recruit through the Owner; sessions ≤45 min; consent recorded.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
Use the `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` review template. Where the standard and the screen catalogue disagree (e.g. politeness level), the standard wins and the catalogue entry is corrected by a docs PR filed from this ticket.

## Test plan
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
N/A — research. Validation is the sign-off, plus the downstream check that E40-Q01 can write the critical-override test matrix directly from Deliverable 2 with no further questions.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
Manual review with an accessibility specialist plus one screen-reader user session over the prototype (NVDA + VoiceOver). Findings tabled with severity (blocker / major / minor) and an owner.

## Security notes
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
Session recordings may show account balances and symbols; store in the private design drive, classify Internal, redact account identifiers in the published report. No credentials are shown to participants.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
Announcement text must not read out anything the visual UI redacts — confirm no channel reads a webhook URL or secret aloud.

## Accessibility notes
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
At least one session includes keyboard-only and screen-reader use of a notification stream, so the a11y strategy in E40-D01 starts from observation rather than from the standard alone.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
This ticket *is* the accessibility note; its output is the a11y contract that E40-S01..S04 implement and E40-Q02 verifies.

## Performance notes
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
The 2 s condition-to-toast budget (SCR-092) is tested for *perceived* adequacy: does a 2 s delay change trader behaviour? Record the answer; it either confirms the budget or escalates it to the Architect.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
Announcement throttling interacts with the 250 ms WS cadence: the documented rule must not require per-message DOM live-region writes at 4 Hz.

## Observability
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
N/A.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
N/A.

## Definition of Done
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
- [ ] Report merged at `docs/design/research/e40-alert-attention.md`.
- [ ] Critical-override list ratified by the Owner, linked from E40-S02 and E40-Q01.
- [ ] Storm threshold and window stated numerically, linked from E40-K01/E40-T03.
- [ ] CDO sign-off comment posted.
- [ ] Findings presented at a design review.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff

- [ ] Accessibility lead sign-off.

## Dependencies

None blocking. Informs E40-D02, E40-D02, E40-K01, E40-T03, E40-S02, E40-Q01.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
`E40-D02`, `E40-D02` — reviews their output. Blocks `E40-D02`.

## Branch

title: Design all five alert surfaces and ship the engineering handoff pack
body:
## Context
This ticket merges the former E40-D02, E40-D02 and E40-D02 into a single design-delivery ticket covering SCR-090, SCR-091, SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 plus the signed-off handoff pack. Design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`): consumed by E40-S01/E40-S01 in Sprint 18, so it must be Done by end of Sprint 16.

### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
SCR-090 and SCR-091 are the authoring surfaces of E40 and both carry explicit design sign-off checklists in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §7. SCR-091 is *not* a new editor: it reuses the rule condition editor (SCR-081, designed in E36-D02) minus the execution-action step, per digest 23 §19 and the CMP-164 AlertBuilderForm contract. This ticket's hardest job is making the reuse obvious — a trader who has authored a rule must recognise the alert editor instantly, while never being able to reach an action step.

Design-ahead: consumed by E40-S01 and E40-S01 in Sprint 18, so this must be Done by end of Sprint 16.
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
Authoring an alert is half the product; being told is the other half. This ticket designs the *delivery* surfaces — the fired toast and its detail drawer (SCR-092), the content of the notification centre drawer that E10 mounted empty (SCR-014), and the notification preference matrix (SCR-115) — plus the three design-system entries (CMP-163 AlertRow, CMP-164 AlertBuilderForm, CMP-165 AlertFiredToastGroup) and the motion spec for arriving/stacking/collapsing notifications.

The governing constraint from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-092 is blunt: the toast is `role="status"`, **not assertive**, so it cannot interrupt order entry. Everything here is designed around not being the most important thing on screen.
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
The design-ahead rule in `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` says no frontend work starts until its design is signed off. E40-S01..S04 start in Sprint 18, so the handoff pack must be Done in Sprint 17. This ticket turns three design tickets' output into one artifact an engineer can build from without asking a question.

## Scope / Deliverables
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
- **SCR-090 Alerts centre** (`/alerts`, tabs Active · Triggered · Snoozed): table columns name, symbol, condition, status, last triggered, delivery channels; `+ New alert`; filters by symbol and status; bulk enable/disable/delete with confirmation; row actions toggle-active, snooze (15 m / 1 h / until tomorrow), duplicate, delete, "show on chart".
  - States: empty ("No alerts yet") · active · triggered (badge) · expired one-shot moved to Triggered · snoozed with remaining time · disabled · delivery-failure chip ("Desktop notification blocked by the OS — enable it in Settings") · loading · error.
  - Alerts depending on estimated detectors carry the "(estimated)" qualifier in the condition cell.
- **SCR-091 Alert editor** (modal): condition builder (CMP-164 composing CMP-140/141/143/144/157 from the rule editor), symbol/interval scope (CMP-219), one-shot vs recurring vs once-per-bar, cooldown, expiry, delivery channels (in-app toast, notification centre, desktop, sound with preview), message template with `{{variable}}` interpolation and a live preview, `test-fire` control, CMP-234 ValidationPanel.
  - Plain-language restatement of the alert ("Notify me when BTCUSDT tape speed rises above 3 sigma").
  - Validation presentations: at least one condition, at least one delivery channel, cooldown ≥5 s, expiry in the future, estimated-metric warning, "Sound requires the desktop shell" note in the browser.
  - Explicit, drawn treatment of the **no-actions boundary**: where a rule editor has an Actions section, the alert editor shows the delivery-channel section with a one-line explanation ("Alerts notify; to act automatically, create a rule").
- Both screens drawn in dark, light and high-contrast themes, at compact and comfortable density, and at 200% zoom.
- Redlines with token names (never raw hex/px), state matrix, and Figma Dev Mode links.
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
- **SCR-092 fired toast + detail drawer**: toast shows alert name, the *actual metric value* that triggered it, symbol/timeframe and time; actions open-chart-at-that-moment, snooze, disable, open detail. Detail drawer shows the full metric snapshot (the `alert_deliveries.context` payload) and a link to the bar. Multiple simultaneous alerts collapse into a counted stack ("3 alerts fired for BTCUSDT").
- **SCR-014 notification centre content**: mixed stream of alert / rule / order / risk / system / recorder items with severity by icon + text; grouped/collapsed repeats ("12 similar alerts"); per-category mute; `Shift+click` marks everything above read; deep-link presentation; empty state ("Nothing yet today"); unread badge; overflow (newest 500, older via `GET /api/v1/notifications`).
- **SCR-115 notifications settings**: full event × channel matrix (in-app toast, notification centre, desktop, sound) per category; per-category sound selection with preview and volume; quiet hours with timezone stated; desktop-permission state (granted / denied / unsupported) with per-platform remediation; the **drawn, non-negotiable** state showing that risk, lockout, kill-switch and rejection notifications cannot be fully muted; test-notification control.
- **Design-system contributions**: CMP-163 AlertRow, CMP-164 AlertBuilderForm and CMP-165 AlertFiredToastGroup specced as catalogue entries (props, variants, states, tokens, Storybook story list) and raised with the design-system team; CMP-045 Toast and CMP-060 NotificationCenter extended only via documented variants, never forked.
- **Motion spec**: toast enter/exit (transform+opacity only so the chart surface never relayouts), stack collapse, unread-badge change, drawer open; `prefers-reduced-motion` variant for each; timings expressed in `motion.*` tokens.
- **Sound assets**: ≤4 sounds, total ≤200 KB, each with a text label; a designed fallback when audio is blocked.
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
- `docs/design/handoff/e40-alerts-handoff.md` containing:
  - Dev Mode links per frame for SCR-090, SCR-091, SCR-092, SCR-014, SCR-115.
  - **Token map**: every colour/space/type/elevation/motion value used, as token names only.
  - **State matrix** per screen: loading · empty · populated · active · triggered · snoozed · expired · disabled · delivery-failed · vocabulary-unavailable · permission-denied (desktop notifications) · error — each with a frame link and the copy string.
  - **Copy deck**: every string, including the estimated-detector qualifier, the "Sound requires the desktop shell" note, the auto-disarm explanation, the storm-summary wording ratified in E40-D01, the locked-row explanation in SCR-115, and all validation messages.
  - **Component contracts** for CMP-163, CMP-164, CMP-165 incl. the agreed Storybook story list.
  - **A11y contract** lifted verbatim from E40-D01: live-region roles, keyboard maps, announcement throttling, focus order.
  - **Motion table**: token, duration, easing, reduced-motion counterpart.
  - **Interaction spec** for snooze durations (15 m / 1 h / until tomorrow), bulk actions and their confirmations, `Shift+click` mark-above-read, and deep-link behaviour from a notification back to the originating chart/rule/order.
  - **Open questions: none** — anything unresolved is either decided here or explicitly deferred with a ticket link.
- Walkthrough session with the two frontend engineers who will build S01..S04, plus QA; recorded.

## Out of scope
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
SCR-092, SCR-014 content and SCR-115 (E40-D02). Motion timing (E40-D02). The a11y review pass itself (E40-D01). Handoff assembly (E40-D02).
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
SCR-090 and SCR-091 (E40-D02). The a11y review pass (E40-D01). Handoff assembly (E40-D02). Shell chrome itself (E10).
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
Building anything. Design QA of the built result (E40-D03).

## Acceptance criteria
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogue checklist item is drawn
  Given the SCR-090 and SCR-091 design sign-off checklists in 14-screens-catalogue.md §7
  When the file is reviewed
  Then every checklist line maps to a named frame in Figma and is ticked in the review comment
Scenario: Composition uses only catalogued components
  When the file is audited against 15-component-catalogue.md
  Then every element resolves to an existing CMP id, or to a documented new/extended entry (CMP-163, CMP-164) raised against the design-system team in E40-D02
Scenario: The action boundary is visible, not implied (edge)
  Given a trader familiar with the rule editor opens the alert editor
  Then no affordance suggests an action can be attached, and the explanatory line is drawn as persistent copy, not a tooltip
Scenario: Failure states are designed (failure)
  Then the vocabulary-unavailable state (metric service offline), the delivery-failure chip and the auto-disarmed state ("metric source unavailable — alert disarmed, here is why", US-ALRT-002) are all drawn
```
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
```gherkin
Scenario: The toast never competes with order entry
  Given the SCR-092 frames
  Then the toast is annotated role="status", is positioned clear of the order ticket region, and no frame shows it taking focus
Scenario: Critical channels are visibly unmutable
  Given the SCR-115 matrix
  Then the risk, lockout, kill-switch and rejection rows are drawn in a locked state with an inline explanation, not merely omitted
Scenario: Sound is never the only channel (failure)
  Given a user disables every visual channel and leaves sound on
  Then the design shows the in-app record persisting regardless, and the matrix prevents a sound-only configuration
Scenario: Reduced motion is designed, not derived
  Then every motion entry has an explicit prefers-reduced-motion counterpart drawn, and the toast reduced-motion variant is fade-only per SCR-015
```
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
```gherkin
Scenario: The pack is self-sufficient
  Given a frontend engineer who has not attended any design review
  When they read the pack
  Then they can enumerate every state, string and token needed for SCR-090, SCR-091, SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 without asking a question
Scenario: Design-ahead is satisfied
  Then the pack is Status Done before Sprint 18 starts, meeting the >=2-sprint design-ahead rule for E40-S01..S04
Scenario: An unresolved decision is visible, not hidden (edge)
  Given a detail was deferred during review
  Then it appears in the pack under "Deferred" with a ticket link and a stated interim behaviour, never as silence
Scenario: Copy is complete (failure)
  Given any state in the state matrix
  Then it has a copy string; an empty cell fails the review
```

## Technical notes / design
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
Reuse the E36 rule-editor Figma library directly rather than copying frames; divergence between the two editors is a defect, not a design choice. The condition row, operand picker and validation panel must be *instances*, not detached copies, so E36 fixes propagate.
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
The detail drawer renders `alert_deliveries.context`, a free-form JSON snapshot; design it as a key-value table (CMP-036 KeyValueRow) with a sensible ordering rule and a graceful presentation for unknown keys, because the context shape varies by metric family and the design cannot enumerate it.
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
Publish the token map as a machine-readable JSON block alongside the prose so the frontend can diff it against the shipped CSS custom properties in E40-D03 rather than comparing screenshots.

## Test plan
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
Design review with the CDO, a frontend lead and QA; the QA reviewer walks the state matrix and confirms every state is reachable and testable. Contrast checked with the design-system contrast tool on every theme.
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
Design review incl. a frontend lead and the design-system owner (for the three CMP entries). Motion reviewed against `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` motion tokens. Storybook story list agreed with engineering so E40-S02 builds exactly those.
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
Reviewed by the two implementing engineers and by QA; QA confirms every state in the matrix is reachable and observable, which is the input to E40-Q01's test plan.

## Security notes
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
The message-template preview must never render a secret-bearing variable. The variable allow-list drawn in the picker is the same allow-list E40-T02 enforces; list it explicitly in the redlines so the two cannot drift.
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
The notification body and the detail drawer must be designed for *untrusted* text: alert names and message templates are user-authored, so the frames must specify plain-text rendering with no markup interpretation and a maximum rendered length with truncation — the visual contract that backs E40-X01's injection controls.
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
The copy deck must specify that user-authored alert names and messages render as plain text with no markup interpretation, and state the truncation limit — the design-side half of E40-X01's injection control.

## Accessibility notes
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
Table semantics drawn (name/symbol/condition/status/last-triggered/delivery as real columns with headers); status is text plus icon, never colour alone; the create button is reachable from the page heading level; focus order annotated on both frames; the sound preview has a text label.
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
SCR-014 is `aria-live="polite"`, escalating to assertive only for order rejects and risk lockouts; absolute timestamps available alongside relative ones; SCR-115 is a checkbox matrix with row and column headers; every sound has a play button with a text label; the notification drawer must not steal focus when it opens on a new event.
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
The a11y contract section is normative, not advisory; E40-Q02 audits against it.

## Performance notes
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
Annotate the SCR-090 list as virtualised and cursor-paginated with ≤1 Hz live updates, and SCR-091 validation as a ≤300 ms round-trip with an explicit pending state so the design does not assume instant validation.
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
SCR-014 annotated as virtualised — 500 rows at ≤8 ms scripting per scroll frame, unread count debounced to 250 ms. Toast render is immediate on the `alerts` WS message; the detail fetch is lazy. Sound assets preloaded once, ≤200 KB total.
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
The pack restates the budgets the design assumes: ≤2 s condition-to-toast, ≤1 Hz list updates, 500-row virtualised centre at ≤8 ms/frame, ≤200 KB sounds, ≤300 ms validation round-trip.

## Observability

Annotate the audited events on the frames: `alert.created`, `alert.updated`, `alert.enabled_changed`, `alert.deleted`.
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs

### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
Lists the analytics and audit events each surface must emit, so instrumentation is built in, not retrofitted.

## Definition of Done
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
- [ ] Both screens hi-fi in all themes/densities, 200% zoom frame included.
- [ ] Every catalogue sign-off checklist line ticked in the review comment.

title: Spike: alert evaluation placement, subscription sharing and storm thresholds
body:
## Context
Alerts must be evaluated server-side so they fire with the client closed (US-ALRT-001 NFR), and must reuse "the same metric catalogue and evaluation engine as the rule engine" (US-ALRT-002 NFR) with "one event bus; no duplicate evaluation" (US-ALRT-003 NFR). Those three constraints leave a real design question open: does M22 run alerts as degenerate rules inside E35's evaluator, or as a separate lightweight evaluator subscribing to the same metric bus?

Getting this wrong is expensive in both directions. Folding alerts into the rule evaluator drags per-rule sandboxing, execution-time budgets and arming semantics onto something that only ever sends a notification. Running a second evaluator risks the duplicate-evaluation the NFR forbids and a slow drift in metric semantics. This spike answers it with measurements before E40-T02/T03 are written.

Timebox: **3 days**, agreed with the Architect. Not expected to produce production code.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Q1** — Placement: prototype both options against E35's `MetricRegistry` and evaluator interfaces (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11) and measure, at 500 armed alerts across 20 symbols under a recorded high-rate window from E16/E26: p50/p95/p99 condition-met → `alert_deliveries` row committed; CPU and RSS delta; number of metric subscriptions created.
- **Q2** — Subscription sharing: does keying subscriptions on `alerts.condition_hash` (already in the schema) collapse duplicate work as expected? Measure the subscription count for a corpus where 100 alerts share 12 distinct conditions.
- **Q3** — Storm thresholds: replay a detector-heavy window (E25 stacked-imbalance events) and measure the natural firing rate distribution, validating or correcting the threshold ratified in E40-D01 (">N deliveries per user per 60 s"), plus the aggregation-window choice.
- **Q4** — `once_per_bar` semantics: confirm the bar-open key can be derived deterministically from the trigger's `timeframe` for every supported timeframe, including when a bar is revised by a late tick.
- **Q5** — Cost of the notify-only IR guard: measure the validation overhead of rejecting action-bearing IR at `POST /api/v1/alerts` against the ≤300 ms budget in SCR-091.
- **Deliverable**: `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0019-alert-evaluation-placement.md` recording the decision with the numbers, plus follow-up notes attached to E40-T02/T03.

## Out of scope
Implementing the chosen design (E40-T03). Delivery-channel transport (E40-T04). Webhook egress (E40-S03).

## Decision criteria (stated up front)
- If the shared-evaluator option adds >15% p99 latency to E35's rule evaluation under the 500-alert load, alerts get their own evaluator subscribing to the same bus.
- If the separate evaluator cannot demonstrably reuse E35's metric registry without duplicating computation (Q2 subscription count > distinct condition hashes), the shared option wins regardless of latency, because the NFR is a correctness constraint, not a performance preference.
- If neither option meets the 1 s condition-to-record budget at 500 alerts, the spike escalates a capacity decision to the Architect rather than picking the least-bad option.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  Then Q1's table reports p50/p95/p99, CPU, RSS and subscription counts for both prototypes under the identical recorded window
Scenario: The decision follows the stated criteria
  Then the ADR names which criterion decided it and shows the number that triggered it
Scenario: Storm threshold is validated against real data (edge)
  Given the detector-heavy replay window
  Then the measured firing-rate distribution either confirms the E40-D01 threshold or the ADR proposes a corrected one with the histogram attached
Scenario: An inconclusive result is recorded as such (failure)
  Given neither option meets the latency budget
  Then the ADR records "defer, need capacity decision" with the evidence, and a follow-up ticket is filed, rather than a decision being asserted without support
```

## Technical notes / design
Prototype on a branch off E35's merged evaluator. Drive load from recorded Parquet windows via the E26 replay harness so runs are reproducible; state the exact window (symbol, date range) in the ADR so the numbers can be re-derived. Measure with the same Prometheus histograms E40-T03 will ship, not with ad hoc timers.

## Test plan
Benchmark harness only, checked in under `benchmarks/alerts/` even though the prototype code is throwaway — the harness is reused by E40-Q02.

## Security notes
The prototype must not reach any external network; webhook egress is explicitly excluded so the spike cannot accidentally establish an SSRF-shaped code path that gets promoted later.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend spike.

## Performance notes
Budgets under test: condition met → in-app record ≤1 s (US-ALRT-001); condition met → visible toast ≤2 s (SCR-092); validation round-trip ≤300 ms (SCR-091).

## Observability
Defines the metric names E40-T03/T04 will ship: `cv_alert_eval_latency_seconds`, `cv_alerts_armed`, `cv_alert_subscriptions`, `cv_alert_suppressed_total{reason}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Q1–Q5 answered with recorded evidence.
- [ ] `ADR-0019-alert-evaluation-placement.md` merged (a "defer" outcome is still an ADR).

title: Write the alert test plan and automate the E2E and contract suites
body:
## Context
Merged from the former E40-Q01 and E40-Q01: the black-box plan and the automation that implements it are one QA slice.

### Part A — Black-box test plan, fixtures and exploratory charters
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires a black-box test plan per feature, written from the specification rather than from the code. Alerts are unusually testable on paper — every trigger mode, gate and channel has a stated behaviour — and unusually easy to get wrong in ways unit tests miss (a cooldown consumed by a snoozed alert, a storm summary that loses a firing, a mute that silences a risk event). This ticket writes the oracle before the implementation is finished.
### Part B — E2E and contract automation for alert authoring, firing and delivery
R3's E2E gate (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4) explicitly names "alert firing" as required Playwright coverage on web *and* Electron. This ticket turns E40-Q01's plan into the automated suites that make the gate real.

## Scope / Deliverables
### Part A — Black-box test plan, fixtures and exploratory charters
- `docs/qa/test-plans/e40-alerts.md` — a black-box plan covering:
  - **Trigger-mode matrix**: `once` / `every_time` / `once_per_bar` × condition-true-once / true-continuously / true-across-a-bar-boundary / true-on-a-revised-bar, with the expected firing count per cell.
  - **Gating matrix**: enabled, deleted, expired, snoozed, muted symbol, muted category, quiet hours, cooldown, storm limit — including the ordering assertion that a snoozed alert does **not** consume its cooldown.
  - **Critical-override matrix**: every entry of the E40-D01 ratified list × every mute/quiet-hours combination, asserting delivery in all cells. This is the test coverage the US-ALRT-006 NFR demands.
  - **Channel matrix**: in-app / desktop (granted, denied, unsupported) / email (success, transient failure, permanent failure) / webhook (flag off in R3) / push (rejected), asserting in every case that the in-app record exists and is unaffected.
  - **Condition-family coverage**: price (US-ALRT-001), indicator/metric (US-ALRT-002), order-flow and detector (US-ALRT-003) — at least one authored alert per family, each with the expected firing against a named recorded window.
  - **History and export**: firing history completeness incl. suppressed entries, 90-day retention expectation, CSV export content.
  - **RBAC/scoping**: own-alerts-only for read, write, ack and delivery listing.
- **Fixtures**: named recorded Bybit windows (from E16/E26) that deterministically produce — (a) a single clean price cross, (b) an RSI bar-close cross, (c) a stacked-imbalance burst suitable for storm testing, (d) a metric-source-loss event for the auto-disarm case. Each fixture documented with symbol, window, expected events and expected firing count.
- **Fault-injection helpers** (shared with E40-D03 and E40-Q02): force delivery-failed, force desktop-permission-denied, force vocabulary-unavailable, force a 412 concurrent edit, force a storm.
- **Exploratory charters** (session-based, 60–90 min each): "author the strangest alert you can and try to make it act"; "make the notification centre lie about the unread count"; "configure yourself into silence and see what still reaches you"; "fire a storm and try to lose a firing"; "break the alert editor with the keyboard only".
- Traceability table mapping every US-ALRT scenario to at least one test case id.
### Part B — E2E and contract automation for alert authoring, firing and delivery
- **Playwright E2E (web + Electron)**, driven against staging (demo) with the E26 replay harness supplying the recorded windows:
  1. *Author and fire a price alert* — create via SCR-091 → appears Active in SCR-090 → replay the window → toast appears with the triggering value → detail drawer shows the metric snapshot → item in SCR-014 → ack → badge clears.
  2. *Indicator alert on bar close* — RSI(14) 15m crosses below 30; assert it fires on bar close and not intrabar, and that the editor stated which.
  3. *Order-flow alert* — stacked imbalance depth ≥3; assert the firing carries the price range, direction and the "(estimated)" qualifier.
  4. *One-shot vs recurring* — one-shot disarms after firing; recurring re-arms after cooldown.
  5. *Snooze and mute* — snooze moves the alert to the Snoozed tab with remaining time; muting ETHUSDT silences sound/desktop while the record persists.
  6. *Critical override* — with everything muted and quiet hours on, a risk notification still delivers (driven by an E39 risk event injected via the fixture).
  7. *Storm* — 25 firings in a minute produce a summary plus individually-recorded suppressed entries, all visible in history.
  8. *Delivery failure* — desktop permission denied shows the blocked chip and remediation; the in-app record is unaffected.
  9. *Bulk actions with a partial failure* — result reported per item.
  10. *Electron-specific* — an OS notification is raised while the window is unfocused and clicking it focuses the window at the right detail.
- **Contract suites**: every `/alerts*` and `/notifications` operation and response code validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml`; the `alerts` WS payload validated against `23-ws-protocol.md` §15.7, including `unacked_count` and the `unacked_only` option; a schema-drift test that fails when implementation and document diverge.
- **Integration suite**: fixture replay → expected firing sequence, run in CI on every push to alert modules; determinism asserted by running the critical fixture twice in one job and diffing the sequences.
- CI wiring: the alert E2E suite runs in the nightly full pass and as a required check on alert-touching PRs; flake budget and quarantine policy per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`.

## Out of scope
### Part A — Black-box test plan, fixtures and exploratory charters
Writing the automation (E40-Q01). Performance/chaos scripts (E40-Q02). A11y audit (E40-Q02). Security abuse cases (E40-X01) — though the plan cross-references them.
### Part B — E2E and contract automation for alert authoring, firing and delivery

### Part A — Black-box test plan, fixtures and exploratory charters
Fixtures are recorded windows, not synthetic streams, so the tests exercise the real ingestion path. Register each fixture in the shared fixture catalogue with a checksum so a silently changed recording fails loudly.

Electron coverage runs against the packaged shell so the IPC notification path is genuinely exercised, not mocked.

Assert on server state as well as UI state (delivery rows, statuses, audit rows) — a UI that looks right over a broken record is exactly the failure mode alerts have.

Fixtures may embed real recorded market data but must contain no account identifiers, keys or balances; scrub and verify before checking in. The fault-injection surface is itself a threat if it reaches production — hence the guard and its test.

title: Run alert perf/storm/chaos and a11y audits, then give QA sign-off
body:
## Context
Merged from the former E40-Q02, E40-Q02 and E40-Q02 — the non-functional verification passes and the QA sign-off that consumes them.

### Part A — Performance, load, storm and chaos scenarios
Alerts have hard latency budgets (≤1 s to record, ≤2 s to toast) and a failure mode — losing or duplicating a notification across a crash — that only chaos testing surfaces. R3's quality gates require load and chaos coverage; this ticket supplies both for E40 and produces the numbers E40-T05 records as the baseline.
### Part B — Accessibility audit against the a11y contract
E40-D01 wrote the a11y contract in Figma; this ticket verifies the built product against it. Notifications are where WCAG 2.2.1 (no timing loss) and 4.1.3 (status messages) are most commonly failed, and R3's a11y gate requires a verified pass before the train closes.
### Part C — Exploratory charters, regression pack and QA sign-off
Epic DoD requires an epic-level QA pass, not just per-child sign-offs. This ticket runs the unscripted testing that finds what the matrices did not, curates what E40 contributes to the permanent regression pack, and records the sign-off that lets the epic close.

## Scope / Deliverables
### Part A — Performance, load, storm and chaos scenarios
- **Load profile (k6 + a backend harness)**, reusing the benchmark harness from E40-K01:
  - 500 armed alerts across 20 symbols under a recorded high-rate window; assert p95 condition-met → `alert_deliveries` committed ≤1 s and p99 ≤2 s;
  - 50 concurrent WS subscribers on the `alerts` topic; assert the 250 ms cadence holds and no subscriber receives a truncated or out-of-order delta;
  - `GET /notifications` at page size 500 against ≥1M rows across the four source tables; assert p95 <200 ms;
  - subscription-sharing assertion: 500 alerts over 40 distinct conditions must create 40 metric subscriptions, not 500.
- **Storm scenario**: drive the stacked-imbalance fixture until the suppressor engages; assert the summary is produced, every individual firing is still recorded, the UI stays responsive (frontend frame budget measured), and `cv_alert_suppressed_total{reason="storm"}` matches the arithmetic exactly.
- **Chaos scenarios** (per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`):
  1. **Kill mid-fire** — SIGKILL the API between the delivery insert and the outbox poller run; on restart assert exactly-once delivery and no lost firing.
  2. **Postgres failover during a firing burst** — assert no duplicate deliveries and no lost outbox rows.
  3. **WS disconnect during a storm** — client reconnects, receives a correct snapshot with an accurate `unacked_count`, and no delivery is lost or double-counted.
  4. **Metric source loss** — the referenced source goes away mid-window; assert auto-disarm with an explanatory delivery, and correct recovery when the source returns.
  5. **Email relay down** — assert per-channel failure isolation: the in-app record is unaffected and one channel-failure notification is raised, not one per attempt.
  6. **Outbox poller stall** — pause the poller, accumulate depth, resume; assert catch-up without duplicates and that the depth alert fired.
- **Soak**: 24 h with 200 armed alerts on the staging demo feed; assert no memory growth beyond the agreed envelope, no outbox dead rows, and no drift between `fire_count` and the delivery row count.
- Results published to the perf dashboard and recorded against `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; a regression gate at +5% p95 wired into the nightly run.
### Part B — Accessibility audit against the a11y contract
- Automated: axe-core across `/alerts`, the SCR-091 modal, the SCR-014 drawer, the SCR-092 detail drawer and the SCR-115 settings section, in dark, light and high-contrast themes, at 100% and 200% zoom — wired as a CI gate for those routes.
- Manual screen-reader passes with **NVDA/Firefox** and **VoiceOver/Safari**, plus the Electron shell, covering:
  - a single firing (is the toast announced politely and does focus stay put?);
  - a burst of 25 firings (does announcement throttling produce a summary rather than a flood?);
  - an order rejection arriving during alert chatter (does it reach the separate `role="alert"` region promptly?);
  - the notification drawer opening on a new event (does it avoid stealing focus?);
  - the settings matrix (are row and column headers announced, and is a locked row announced as locked with its reason?).
- **Keyboard-only sweep**: every action in every surface reachable and operable without a mouse — tabs, filters, bulk selection, row actions, snooze menu, editor authoring end to end, mark-all-read, `Shift+click` equivalent, sound preview, quiet-hours fields.
- **Timing audit (WCAG 2.2.1)**: every auto-dismissing toast proven to have a persistent record; pause-on-hover/focus verified; no information exists only transiently.
- **Non-colour encoding** verification for severity, status, snoozed, disabled and delivery-failed.
- Contrast measurement of every state in every theme, including focus rings at ≥3:1.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` verification on toast, stack collapse and drawer.
- Findings logged with WCAG references and severity; blockers/majors fixed inside E40, minors triaged into E47.
- Report at `docs/qa/a11y/e40-alerts-audit.md`.
### Part C — Exploratory charters, regression pack and QA sign-off
- Execute the five exploratory charters from E40-Q01 as timeboxed session-based tests (60–90 min each), against staging (demo) with the replay harness:
  1. "Author the strangest alert you can and try to make it act" — the invariant hunt.
  2. "Make the notification centre lie about the unread count."
  3. "Configure yourself into silence and see what still reaches you" — the critical-override hunt.
  4. "Fire a storm and try to lose a firing."
  5. "Break the alert editor with the keyboard only."
- Session sheets recorded (charter, duration, areas covered, bugs, questions, follow-up charters spawned) per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`'s session-based model.
- **Regression pack curation**: select the subset of E40-Q01/Q03 tests that enter the permanent regression suite — at minimum the invariant test (an alert cannot act), the critical-override matrix, exactly-once-under-restart, and the storm-conservation assertion — and wire them into the release regression job.
- Defect triage: every finding filed with `priority/*`, a repro, and the layer that should have caught it (feeding the test-gap analysis); P0/P1 fixed before the epic closes.
- **Epic-level QA sign-off comment** on E40 recording pass/fail per US-ALRT story, the residual risk, and any explicit deviation (e.g. webhook untested because it is flagged off and descoped to R5).
- Contribution to the R3 exit-criteria evidence pack: the alert-firing E2E coverage named in §7.4.

## Out of scope
### Part A — Performance, load, storm and chaos scenarios
Functional E2E (E40-Q01), a11y (E40-Q02), security abuse cases (E40-X01). Webhook egress load (E40-S03, R5).
### Part B — Accessibility audit against the a11y contract
Functional testing (E40-Q01). Design fidelity (E40-D03). Non-alert surfaces.
### Part C — Exploratory charters, regression pack and QA sign-off
Writing new automation (E40-Q01). Fixing defects (the owning ticket does that). Security sign-off (E40-X01).

## Acceptance criteria
### Part A — Performance, load, storm and chaos scenarios
```gherkin
Scenario: Latency budgets hold under load
  Given 500 armed alerts across 20 symbols on the recorded high-rate window
  Then p95 condition-to-record is at most 1 s and p99 at most 2 s, recorded in the perf dashboard
Scenario: Exactly-once survives a kill
  Given the API is SIGKILLed between the delivery insert and dispatch
  When it restarts
  Then the pending outbox row is delivered exactly once and no firing is lost
Scenario: A storm never loses a firing (edge)
  Given 25 qualifying firings inside 60 s
  Then the suppressed count plus the delivered count equals 25 exactly, and all 25 are retrievable from history
Scenario: Subscription sharing does not regress (failure)
  Given 500 alerts over 40 distinct conditions
  Then exactly 40 metric subscriptions exist; a higher number fails the run
Scenario: A soak reveals no drift (edge)
  Given the 24 h soak
  Then fire_count equals the delivery-row count for every alert, memory is within envelope, and there are no dead outbox rows
```
### Part B — Accessibility audit against the a11y contract
```gherkin
Scenario: Automated checks are clean
  When axe-core runs across the five surfaces in every theme at 100% and 200% zoom
  Then there are zero serious or critical violations, and the check is wired as a CI gate
Scenario: A burst does not flood the screen reader
  Given 25 alerts fire within a minute with a screen reader active
  Then a summary is announced rather than 25 individual announcements, and the items remain individually readable on demand
Scenario: A critical rejection is not queued behind chatter (edge)
  Given a stream of alert toasts and an order rejection
  Then the rejection is announced through the separate assertive region without waiting for the polite queue to drain
Scenario: Nothing is lost to timing (failure)
  Given any auto-dismissing toast
  Then its content is demonstrably retrievable from the notification centre afterwards
Scenario: A locked preference row is understandable (edge)
  Given the risk-events row in the settings matrix
  Then the screen reader announces it as locked and conveys why, not merely as disabled
```
### Part C — Exploratory charters, regression pack and QA sign-off
```gherkin
Scenario: All charters are executed and recorded
  Then five session sheets exist, each with its charter, duration, coverage notes and findings
Scenario: The regression pack is wired and green
  Then the selected tests run in the release regression job and pass on the release candidate
Scenario: Every Must story has an explicit verdict
  Then the sign-off comment records pass or fail for US-ALRT-001 through US-ALRT-006 individually, with evidence links
Scenario: A P1 defect blocks sign-off (failure)
  Given an open P0 or P1 defect in E40 scope
  Then QA sign-off is withheld and the epic cannot reach Done
Scenario: Untested scope is declared, not implied (edge)
  Given webhook delivery is flagged off and descoped to R5
  Then the sign-off states it explicitly as untested-by-design with the descoping reference, rather than silently omitting it
```

## Technical notes / design
### Part A — Performance, load, storm and chaos scenarios
Chaos uses the existing fault-injection framework (process kill, container pause, Postgres failover via the compose topology) rather than in-code hooks, so the tests exercise real failure rather than a simulation of it.

Exactly-once is asserted from the data, not from logs: count delivery rows per firing and assert the outbox `(topic, dedup_key)` uniqueness held.

The frontend frame-budget measurement during the storm uses the same tracing approach as the chart-engine benchmarks so the numbers are comparable.
### Part B — Accessibility audit against the a11y contract
Test against the built application on staging (demo) with the E40-Q01 fault-injection helpers driving the burst, the rejection and the permission-denied states — the hard-to-reach states are exactly the ones most likely to be inaccessible.

Verify against the E40-D01 contract document clause by clause; a contract clause with no corresponding verification step is itself a finding.
### Part C — Exploratory charters, regression pack and QA sign-off
Run charters against a realistic data state (a populated alert set, a busy notification history), not an empty install — the interesting defects in a notification system appear at volume.

Spawn follow-up charters when a session finds a rich seam; record them even if they cannot be run within the sprint, so R5 hardening inherits a concrete list.

## Test plan
### Part A — Performance, load, storm and chaos scenarios
The scripts are the deliverable. Validate them by mutation: remove the outbox dedup index in a scratch environment and confirm the exactly-once test fails; disable the suppressor and confirm the storm test fails.
### Part B — Accessibility audit against the a11y contract
Automated axe-core plus scripted manual passes with recorded evidence (screen-reader transcripts and short screen recordings attached to the ticket).
### Part C — Exploratory charters, regression pack and QA sign-off
This ticket executes tests rather than defining them. Its own quality check is the test-gap analysis: for each defect found exploratorily, name the automated layer that should have caught it and file the automation gap.

## Security notes
### Part A — Performance, load, storm and chaos scenarios
Load scripts run against staging (demo) with demo credentials only. Generated load must respect the exchange rate-limit governor — a load test that trips Bybit's connection limits is a self-inflicted incident, so connection counts are bounded and documented.
### Part B — Accessibility audit against the a11y contract

### Part C — Exploratory charters, regression pack and QA sign-off

## Accessibility notes

### Part B — Accessibility audit against the a11y contract
