title: Ship the SCR-090 alerts centre and the SCR-091 alert editor
body:
## Context
Merged from the former E40-S01 and E40-S01 — the two authoring/management surfaces ship as one frontend slice against the same CMP-163/CMP-164 contracts and the same `/alerts` API.

### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
US-ALRT-004 asks for "one place listing all alerts and their history, so that I manage them coherently". That place is SCR-090 at `/alerts`, with tabs **Active · Triggered · Snoozed**. It is also where US-ALRT-001's "recorded in the alert centre", US-ALRT-003's storm-suppression visibility and US-ALRT-006's snooze affordances become real.

Design contract: `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-090 and the E40-D02 handoff pack.
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
This is where US-ALRT-001 (price), US-ALRT-002 (indicator/metric) and US-ALRT-003 (order-flow/detector) become authorable. SCR-091 explicitly *reuses the rule condition editor (SCR-081) minus execution actions* — CMP-164 AlertBuilderForm composes CMP-140/141/143/144/157 from E36. The story's value is that a trader who can write a rule can write an alert instantly, and can never accidentally write an alert that trades.

## Scope / Deliverables
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
- Route `/alerts` (SCR-090), RBAC-gated on `alerts:read`; write affordances hidden without `alerts:write` and the API's 403 surfaced as an explanatory state rather than a dead button.
- Table (CMP-049) of alerts with columns **name · symbol · condition · status · last triggered · delivery channels**, rendered from `GET /api/v1/alerts`; each row is **CMP-163 AlertRow**. Status is text plus icon, never colour alone.
- Tabs Active · Triggered · Snoozed; filters by symbol and status (CMP-055 FilterBar); cursor pagination.
- Row actions: toggle active (`PUT /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}/enabled`), snooze 15 m / 1 h / until tomorrow, duplicate (prefills SCR-091), delete (`DELETE`), "show on chart" (deep-link to the chart at the alert's symbol with the level drawn).
- Bulk selection with disarm / delete / mute applied to the selection, each behind a confirmation that names the count and the consequence, with the **result reported per item** (US-ALRT-004 scenario 2) — a partial failure lists which items failed and why.
- Firing history per alert: expand a row or open the detail to see firings with timestamps and the values at fire time, sourced from `GET /api/v1/alerts/deliveries?alert_id=…`, **exportable** as CSV (US-ALRT-004 scenario 3); history is retained ≥90 days by the retention policy.
- Storm-suppression visibility: suppressed firings appear in history with their suppressed status and the summary they were folded into.
- Estimated-detector alerts render the "(estimated)" qualifier on the condition cell (US-ALRT-003 scenario 2).
- Live updates over the WS `alerts` topic at ≤1 Hz; auto-disarmed alerts (metric source unavailable) show the reason inline.
- States from the handoff pack: empty ("No alerts yet") · loading · populated · triggered badge · expired one-shot in Triggered · snoozed with remaining time · disabled · delivery-failure chip ("Desktop notification blocked by the OS — enable it in Settings") · error.
- `+ New alert` opens SCR-091 (E40-S01); until that ships behind its flag, the button is present and disabled with a stated reason.
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
- **CMP-164 AlertBuilderForm** organism and the SCR-091 modal, reachable from SCR-090 `+ New alert`, from a row's Duplicate, from the indicator settings Alerts tab (SCR-069 → "create alert from this indicator", US-IND-008), from the big-trades panel (US-BIG-005) and from the detector panels' "create alert from this threshold/level" affordances (E25 SCR-055/056/057).
- Sections: **Scope** (symbol via CMP-219 SymbolPicker, optional interval, optional account) → **Condition** (CMP-157 MetricPickerCombobox + operand rows + grouping, instances of the E36 components) → **Trigger mode** (once / every time / once per bar, with the bar-close-vs-intrabar semantics displayed explicitly per US-ALRT-002 scenario 3) → **Timing** (cooldown seconds, optional expiry) → **Delivery** (in-app toast, notification centre, desktop, sound with a preview button) → **Message** (template with `{{variable}}` interpolation and a live preview) → **Options** (name, severity).
- **Plain-language restatement** of the alert, rendered from the compiled IR ("Notify me when BTCUSDT tape speed rises above 3 sigma"), wired as the form's accessible description.
- **CMP-234 ValidationPanel** fed by `POST /api/v1/alerts` 422 `RuleIrInvalid` responses: errors first, each entry a button that moves focus to the offending row, error count announced on recompile.
- Client-side validation mirroring the server: ≥1 condition, ≥1 delivery channel, cooldown ≥5 s, expiry in the future; the server remains authoritative and its message wins on conflict.
- **The action boundary**: no actions section exists; the delivery section carries the persistent explanatory line from the copy deck ("Alerts notify; to act automatically, create a rule") linking to `/rules`.
- Estimated-metric warning banner when a selected metric is heuristic (US-ALRT-003 scenario 2).
- "Sound requires the desktop shell" note when running in a browser; sound is never selectable as the only channel.
- **Test-fire** control: produces a delivery through the real path marked as a test, so the user can verify their channel configuration.
- Save paths: `POST /api/v1/alerts` (create, with `Idempotency-Key`), `PUT /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}` with `If-Match` (edit), rendering 412 as "this alert was changed elsewhere — reload and reapply", never last-writer-wins.
- States: draft · validating · valid · invalid · saving · vocabulary-unavailable (metric service offline → editor read-only with an explanation) · permission-denied.

## Out of scope
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
The alert editor modal (E40-S01). The fired toast and notification-centre content (E40-S02). Notification preferences (E40-S02). Any alert-to-action binding (US-ALRT-007, not in E40).
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
The alerts list (E40-S01). Toast/detail (E40-S02). Preferences (E40-S02). Webhook channel selection — hidden behind the `alerts.webhook_enabled` flag until E40-S03 (R5). Any action binding (US-ALRT-007).

## Acceptance criteria
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
```gherkin
Scenario: The list shows everything the story asks for
  Given three alerts in different states
  When I open /alerts
  Then each row shows its condition, symbol, status, last fire time and delivery channels, and the status is readable as text
Scenario: Bulk actions report their result
  Given I select five alerts and choose Disarm
  When one of them fails server-side
  Then four are shown disarmed, the failure is listed with its reason, and the list state matches the server after a refresh
Scenario: History is complete and exportable
  Given an alert that has fired twelve times, three of them suppressed by the storm limiter
  Then the history shows all twelve with timestamps and fire-time values, marks the three as suppressed with a link to their summary, and exports the same twelve rows to CSV
Scenario: A snoozed alert states its remaining time (edge)
  When I snooze an alert for one hour
  Then it moves to the Snoozed tab and displays the remaining time, updating without a page reload
Scenario: A dead metric source is explained, not hidden (failure)
  Given an alert auto-disarmed because its metric source became unavailable
  Then the row shows disarmed with the stated reason, and re-enabling is offered but warns the source is still unavailable
Scenario: Read-only users cannot mutate (failure)
  Given a session without alerts:write
  Then toggle, snooze, delete and bulk controls are absent, and a direct API attempt returns 403 which the UI renders as an explanation
```
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
```gherkin
Scenario: A price alert is authored and saved
  Given I pick BTCUSDT, last price, crosses above, 65000, trigger mode once, channels in-app and desktop
  When I save
  Then POST /api/v1/alerts returns 201, the plain-language restatement reads back the alert, and it appears Active in SCR-090
Scenario: An indicator alert states its evaluation semantics
  Given "RSI(14) on 15m crosses below 30"
  Then the trigger mode section shows it evaluates on bar close by default and offers an explicit intrabar option
Scenario: The editor cannot express an action (edge)
  When I inspect every control and every keyboard path in the modal
  Then no control adds an execution action, and the delivery section explains where actions live
Scenario: Server validation is surfaced actionably (failure)
  Given a condition referencing a metric with no data source
  When I save
  Then the ValidationPanel shows the server's message, focus can be moved to the offending row from the panel, and nothing is persisted
Scenario: A concurrent edit does not overwrite (failure)
  Given the alert was changed in another session after I opened it
  When I save
  Then 412 is rendered as a reload-and-reapply explanation and my payload is not applied
Scenario: A sound-only configuration is refused (edge)
  When I deselect every visual channel and leave sound enabled
  Then saving is blocked with the message that sound may never be the only channel
```

## Technical notes / design
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
Data layer: TanStack Query with the `alerts` WS topic as the invalidation source — the socket carries deliveries and the unacked count, and a delivery for an alert invalidates that alert's row rather than refetching the page. Throttle applied updates to 1 Hz per the screen's performance note.

Snooze is a client-computed `snoozed_until` sent to `PUT /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}`; "until tomorrow" resolves against the user's timezone and is displayed as an absolute time on hover so the relative label is never the only information.

Bulk actions issue individual requests with bounded concurrency and aggregate the outcomes; there is no bulk endpoint in the OpenAPI document and this story does not invent one.
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
Import the E36 condition-editor components as instances from `packages/rule-editor-core`; do **not** fork them. The alert editor passes a `mode: "alert"` capability object that omits the action vocabulary — the omission is a property of the shared component's configuration, and a unit test asserts that in `mode: "alert"` the action vocabulary is empty regardless of what the server returns.

Validation is debounced and calls the same vocabulary/validation service the rule editor uses, so the two editors cannot report different diagnostics for the same condition.

Entry points from indicator, big-trade and detector panels prefill scope and metric via a typed `AlertDraft` object rather than by URL string-building.

## Test plan
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
- Unit (Vitest + RTL): row rendering per state; snooze duration arithmetic incl. the timezone boundary; bulk-result aggregation with a mixed success/failure set; filter and tab derivation; CSV export content.
- Contract: MSW handlers generated from the OpenAPI document; a test fails if the client sends a parameter the spec does not define.
- E2E (Playwright, E40-Q01): create → fire → appears in Triggered → snooze → Snoozed tab → delete.
- Perf: 1 000-alert list scrolls at ≥55 fps with virtualisation; live-update throttling verified at 1 Hz under a firing burst.
- a11y: axe-core green; keyboard-only path through tabs, filters, selection and row actions.
- Coverage ≥80% frontend.
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
- Unit: capability-object test (action vocabulary empty in alert mode); validation mirroring; sound-only refusal; expiry/cooldown boundary values; 412 handling; `AlertDraft` prefill from each entry point.
- Contract: request bodies validated against `AlertInput` in the OpenAPI document.
- E2E (E40-Q01): author a price alert, an RSI alert and a stacked-imbalance alert; test-fire each; verify each fires against a replayed window.
- a11y: axe-core green; keyboard-complete authoring with no mouse; ValidationPanel focus movement verified with a screen reader.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
The condition cell renders user-authored text: render as plain text with no markup interpretation and the truncation limit from the copy deck. Never display `webhook_url` or any secret — the API does not return them, and a test asserts the row component has no code path that would render them if it did. Cross-user access is prevented server-side; the UI must not construct alert ids from any client-held value other than the list response.
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
The message-template field is user input that is later rendered in a toast, a notification row and (eventually) a webhook payload: the editor renders its preview as plain text only, and the placeholder picker offers only the allow-listed namespace enforced by E40-T02. The editor must never accept a free-typed placeholder that bypasses the picker without re-validation. Test-fire goes through the authenticated API, not a client-side shortcut, so it cannot be used to forge a delivery. The webhook URL field stays behind its flag and is not implemented here — no client code path may write `webhook_url` in R3.

## Accessibility notes
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
Per the E40-D01 contract: a real `<table>` with header cells (name, symbol, condition, status, last triggered, delivery); status conveyed as text; the create button reachable from the page heading level; bulk selection announced as "N selected"; tab list is a real `role="tablist"` with arrow-key navigation; live row updates use `aria-live="polite"` with announcement throttling so a burst does not flood; snooze remaining time exposed as text, not only as a progress ring.
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
Per E40-D01: keyboard-complete authoring is a hard requirement (the editor is also the accessible path for creating alerts from canvas surfaces); the plain-language restatement is the form's accessible description; ValidationPanel is `role="log"` with errors first and focus-moving entries; sound preview has a text label and is never the only channel; modal is a focus-trapped dialog with a heading; 200% zoom supported.

## Performance notes
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
List virtualised and cursor-paginated; live updates ≤1 Hz (SCR-090 performance note); no layout thrash on update — row updates mutate text nodes only.
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
Validation round-trip ≤300 ms p95 (SCR-091); no evaluation runs until saved; the metric combobox is virtualised over the full metric catalogue.

## Observability
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
Emit `alerts.list_viewed`, `alerts.filtered`, `alert.enabled_changed`, `alert.snoozed`, `alert.deleted`, `alerts.bulk_action` (analytics); the audited events are emitted server-side and are not duplicated client-side.
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
`alert.editor_opened`, `alert.condition_changed`, `alert.test_fired`, `alert.save_failed{reason}` (analytics); `alert.created` / `alert.updated` are audited server-side.

## Definition of Done
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by automated tests (unit/E2E) or an executed QA step with a follow-up automation ticket.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on the touched frontend package.

title: Ship fired-alert toasts, SCR-092/SCR-014 content and SCR-115 preferences
body:
## Context
Merged from the former E40-S02 and E40-S02 — the delivery-consumption surfaces (toast, detail view, notification centre) and the preference surface that governs them ship as one frontend slice.

### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
US-ALRT-005 (Must half): "a toast appears with the alert detail and an action to open the relevant chart", plus a desktop notification via the Electron shell even when the window is unfocused. US-ALRT-004's alert-centre record and US-OBS-004's system notifications share one surface: SCR-014, the right-rail drawer E10 mounted empty. This story fills all of it.

The governing a11y constraint is that the toast is `role="status"` — it must not interrupt order entry — while order rejects and risk lockouts route to CMP-212's separate `role="alert"` region.
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
US-ALRT-006 (Should) is the counterweight to everything else in E40: snooze, mute and quiet hours exist so the trader is not overwhelmed. Its third scenario is the one that matters most — *a risk alert (daily loss, liquidation proximity, connection loss) always delivers, regardless of mute or quiet hours* — and its NFR requires the critical-override list to be "explicit, documented and covered by tests". That list was ratified in E40-D01 and is implemented here and in E40-T03.

## Scope / Deliverables
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
- **SCR-015 / CMP-165 AlertFiredToastGroup**: a Toast (CMP-045) variant for fired alerts that batches rapid duplicates into one counted summary ("3 alerts fired for BTCUSDT"). Content shows the alert name, **the actual metric value that fired it**, symbol/timeframe and time. Actions: open chart at that moment, snooze, disable, open detail. At most 3 toasts on screen; overflow collapses into a counted stack; errors never auto-dismiss; every toast is duplicated into SCR-014.
- **SCR-092 detail drawer** (CMP-046): the full metric snapshot from `alert_deliveries.context` rendered as a key-value table (CMP-036) with the ordering rule from the handoff pack and a graceful presentation of unknown keys, plus a link to the bar and a "create a rule from this alert" link-out to `/rules/new` prefilled (the link only — E40 never binds an action).
- **SCR-014 notification centre content** inside CMP-209 RightRail, using CMP-060 NotificationCenter: a mixed stream of alert / rule / order / risk / system / recorder items from `GET /api/v1/notifications` (scroll-back) and the `alerts`, `rules`, `orders`, `system` WS topics (live). Severity by icon + text; grouped/collapsed repeats ("12 similar alerts"); per-category mute entry point into SCR-115; `Shift+click` marks everything above read; deep-link to the source (chart at timestamp / rule / order); empty state ("Nothing yet today"); unread badge; overflow keeps the newest 500 with older items reachable via history.
- **Acknowledgement**: mark-read wired to `POST /api/v1/alerts/deliveries/{deliveryId}/ack` and `…/ack-all`; the unacked badge count comes from the `AlertUpdate.unacked_count` field, not a client-side count.
- **Electron desktop notifications**: on an `alerts` delivery with the `desktop` channel, the shell raises an OS notification even when unfocused; clicking it focuses the window and opens the detail. The OS permission state (granted / denied / unsupported) is reported back so SCR-090 and SCR-115 can show the blocked chip and remediation.
- **Delivery-failure surfacing** (US-ALRT-005 scenario 3): a failed channel shows its failure on the alert record while the in-app record persists — the UI must make it obvious that the alert *did* fire and only a channel failed.
- Storm summaries render as a single grouped item that expands to the individual suppressed firings.
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
- **SCR-115 Notifications settings** section under `/settings`: a full **event × channel matrix** (rows: alerts, rule actions, order rejects, risk events, system health, recorder; columns: in-app toast, notification centre, desktop, sound) as labelled checkboxes with row and column headers.
- Per-category **sound selection** with a preview button and volume; assets preloaded once, ≤200 KB total.
- **Quiet hours**: start/end with the timezone stated explicitly, and a permanently visible statement that critical events still notify.
- **Critical-override rows rendered locked**: risk, lockout, kill-switch and order-rejection categories cannot be fully muted; the locked state is drawn with an inline explanation, not silently omitted. Attempting to mute a risk channel is **audited** as `notifications.risk_channel_muted` at high severity.
- **Desktop permission state**: granted / denied / unsupported, with per-platform remediation instructions and a re-request action where the platform allows it.
- **Test-notification control** per channel, so a configuration can be verified without waiting for a real firing.
- **Symbol mute** (US-ALRT-006 scenario 2): muting a symbol records its alerts but produces no sound or notification, and the mute is **visible on the symbol** wherever it appears (watchlist row, chart header, alert row).
- **Snooze** surface consistency: the snooze durations offered here match SCR-090's (15 m / 1 h / until tomorrow) and share one implementation.
- Preferences are local-first and synced through the settings store (E13/`/settings` API); the server-side evaluator reads them so muting works even when the client is closed.

## Out of scope
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
Notification preferences, mute and quiet hours (E40-S02) — this story consumes the preference values but does not provide the editing UI. The alerts list and editor (E40-S01/S02). Webhook (E40-S03).
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
The notification surfaces themselves (E40-S02). Alert-level snooze on a single alert (E40-S01). Appearance/a11y settings (E13). The server-side gating implementation (E40-T03) — this story provides the values it reads.

## Acceptance criteria
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
```gherkin
Scenario: A firing produces a toast with real data
  Given an armed alert fires on BTCUSDT
  When the alerts WS message arrives
  Then a toast appears within 2 s of the condition being met showing the alert name and the triggering metric value, with an action that opens the chart at that moment
Scenario: The toast does not interrupt order entry
  Given focus is inside the order ticket
  When an alert toast appears
  Then focus does not move, the toast is announced politely, and the ticket remains operable
Scenario: Nothing is lost if a toast is missed
  Given a toast auto-dismisses before I read it
  Then the same item is present in the notification centre with its full detail, satisfying WCAG 2.2.1
Scenario: Rapid duplicates collapse (edge)
  Given five alerts fire for BTCUSDT within two seconds
  Then one counted summary toast is shown, expanding to the five individual items, and all five exist separately in the centre
Scenario: A blocked desktop notification is explained (failure)
  Given the OS has denied notification permission
  Then the delivery is shown failed with the reason, the in-app record still exists, and SCR-090 shows the remediation chip
Scenario: Acking is reflected everywhere (edge)
  When I mark everything read
  Then ack-all is called once, the unacked badge reaches zero from the server-provided count, and a reload shows the same state
```
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
```gherkin
Scenario: Muting a symbol silences without losing the record
  Given I mute ETHUSDT
  When an ETHUSDT alert fires
  Then no sound or desktop notification is produced, the delivery is still recorded and visible in the centre, and the mute is shown on the symbol
Scenario: Quiet hours suppress the optional channels only
  Given quiet hours are 22:00 to 07:00 in my stated timezone
  When a normal alert fires at 23:00
  Then desktop and sound are suppressed while the in-app record is created
Scenario: A critical event overrides everything (edge)
  Given quiet hours are active, every symbol is muted and every optional channel is off
  When a daily-loss breach, liquidation-proximity, connection-loss or kill-switch notification is raised
  Then it is delivered on the channels the override list specifies
Scenario: Muting a risk channel is refused and audited (failure)
  When I attempt to disable the risk-event row
  Then the control is locked with an explanation, and any API-level attempt is rejected and audited as notifications.risk_channel_muted
Scenario: A denied OS permission is actionable (failure)
  Given the OS has denied notification permission
  Then the desktop column shows denied with platform-specific remediation, and the test-notification control explains it cannot succeed until permission is granted
Scenario: Sound cannot become the only channel (edge)
  When I disable every visual channel for a category and leave sound on
  Then the change is refused with the message that sound may never be the only channel
```

## Technical notes / design
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
One WS subscription per topic at the shell level, fanned out through a notification store; the store keeps the newest 500 items and falls back to `GET /api/v1/notifications` for scroll-back with the shared `(ts, id)` cursor. Toast presentation subscribes to the store, so a toast and a centre row are two views of one item and can never disagree.

Desktop notifications use the Electron `Notification` API from the main process via the existing IPC bridge from E10; the renderer never calls it directly. The permission outcome is posted back to the server so the delivery status is accurate rather than optimistic.

Deep-links use the E10 deep-link parameter contract (`docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §7), not hand-built URLs.
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
The critical-override list is a **single shared constant** consumed by the server evaluator (E40-T03), the settings UI and the test suite; it is defined once in the shared schema package and imported, never re-declared — that is how the NFR's "explicit, documented and covered by tests" is mechanically guaranteed. A test enumerates the constant and asserts every entry is rendered locked in the matrix.

Quiet hours are stored with an explicit IANA timezone, not an offset, so DST transitions behave; the server evaluates them in that zone.

Symbol mute lives in the same preference document so the evaluator can apply it server-side; the "visible on the symbol" requirement is satisfied by a shared mute-indicator component consumed by the watchlist row, chart header and alert row.

## Test plan
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
- Unit: toast batching/collapse arithmetic; store eviction at 500 with history fallback; unacked-count sourcing (a test asserts the badge never derives from a client-side count); deep-link construction per source kind; unknown-key rendering in the detail table.
- Integration: Electron notification path with permission granted / denied / unsupported (mocked main process).
- E2E (E40-Q01): fire an alert against a replayed window → toast appears → open detail → chart opens at the right timestamp → item present in the centre → ack → badge clears.
- Perf: 500 rows virtualised at ≤8 ms scripting per scroll frame; toast animation asserted to use transform/opacity only (no layout) via a performance trace; unread count debounced to 250 ms.
- a11y: axe-core; screen-reader pass over a burst; reduced-motion variant.
- Coverage ≥80%.
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours

- E2E (E40-Q01): mute a symbol, fire an alert, assert silence plus a recorded delivery; then fire a risk notification and assert it still delivers.
- a11y: axe-core; matrix navigable with row/column headers announced; sound previews labelled.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
Alert names, message templates and rule text are user-authored and arrive over WS: render as plain text with the copy-deck truncation; no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` anywhere in this story — enforced by an ESLint rule and a unit test. The detail drawer renders a free-form `context` object: render values as strings, never evaluate, and cap the rendered depth/size so a large context cannot freeze the renderer. Deep-links must validate their parameters against the E10 contract before navigating, so a crafted notification cannot drive navigation to an arbitrary route.
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
Muting risk notifications is a plausible **abuse path** — a compromised or careless session could silence the very signals that reveal a problem — which is why the override list is enforced server-side, the locked rows cannot be bypassed by an API call, and every attempt is audited at high severity. Preferences are per-user and `scope: self`; one user cannot mute another's notifications. Remediation instructions must not tell a user to disable OS-level security features.

## Accessibility notes
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
Per E40-D01: toast is `role="status"` (polite) and never steals focus; errors/rejections route to CMP-212's separate `role="alert"` region; SCR-014 is `aria-live="polite"` escalating to assertive only for order rejects and risk lockouts; announcement throttling summarises bursts instead of reading each item; absolute timestamps available alongside relative; the drawer does not steal focus when it opens on a new event; every auto-dismissing item has a persistent backstop; `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured (fade only).
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
The matrix uses real row and column headers so a screen reader announces "Risk events, desktop, checked, locked"; sound choices have a play button with a text label; quiet-hours fields state the timezone in text; the locked state is conveyed by text and `aria-disabled` with an `aria-describedby` explanation, never by colour or a cursor change alone.

## Performance notes
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
Condition met → visible toast ≤2 s end to end (SCR-092); centre renders 500 notifications at ≤8 ms scripting per scroll frame (SCR-014); unread count debounced to 250 ms; toast animation must not trigger layout on the chart surface.
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
Sound assets preloaded once, ≤200 KB total, so a triggered alert plays without fetch latency (SCR-115 performance note). Preference writes are debounced and local-first so the matrix never feels laggy.

## Observability

`alert.toast_shown`, `alert.toast_actioned`, `alert.detail_opened`, `alert.snoozed`, `notifications.opened`, `notifications.filtered`, `notifications.item_actioned`, `notifications.mark_all_read` (analytics). Client error reporting for a failed desktop-notification path.

`notifications.preference_changed {event, channel, enabled}` (analytics); `notifications.risk_channel_muted` (**audited**, high severity); `notifications.test_sent {channel}`.

## Definition of Done
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
- [ ] All scenarios automated or QA-executed with follow-ups filed.
- [ ] No-raw-HTML lint rule and test in place.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80%; axe-core green; screen-reader burst pass recorded.

## Dependencies

`E40-T04` (deliveries + `alerts` WS topic + ack endpoints), `E40-D02` (handoff), `E10` (RightRail, ToastHost, IPC bridge, deep-link contract), `E39` (risk notifications that route to the assertive region).

title: Ship HMAC-signed webhook alert delivery with allow-listed egress
body:
## Context
Re-keyed from the former E40-S03 during the roadmap-sizing consolidation. Remains **deferred to R5** per `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §12 descoping-ladder row 6 — it is carried in Backlog and does not consume the R3 sprint window or the 21-point R3 allocation beyond its 1-point placeholder.

US-ALRT-008 is a **Could**, and `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §12 descoping ladder row 6 names "Webhook alert delivery — E40" as descoped from R3 to **R5**, gated on the pen-test and the Live gate (E43/E44). It is specified here so it is ready to pull forward if capacity allows, and so nothing in R3 is built in a way that makes it hard.

Webhook egress is the only part of E40 that makes an outbound network call, which makes it the only part with a real SSRF surface. That is precisely why it is last.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `webhook` channel adapter for the E40-T04 dispatcher, behind feature flag `alerts.webhook_enabled` (default **off** in every environment until R5).
- **Egress policy** (the core of this story):
  - the endpoint must resolve to the Tailscale network by default; a public-internet endpoint is **refused** unless the owner explicitly allow-lists it and acknowledges a warning (US-ALRT-008 scenario 2);
  - DNS resolution is performed once and the resolved IP is the one connected to (pin the resolution, defeating DNS-rebinding);
  - deny loopback, link-local, cloud-metadata and RFC1918 ranges outside the Tailscale CIDR, and refuse redirects entirely;
  - scheme restricted to https except for the Tailscale CIDR where http is permitted with an acknowledgement;
  - a per-endpoint concurrency and rate cap so a webhook cannot be used to amplify traffic.
- **Signing**: payloads are HMAC-SHA256 signed with a per-alert secret stored in `alerts.webhook_secret_enc` via the E27 credential broker; the signature and a timestamp travel in headers, and a replay window is documented for the receiver.
- **Payload**: the alert name, symbol, condition summary, the firing values from `alert_deliveries.context`, the delivery id and the fired-at timestamp — and **never** secrets, API keys, account credentials or account balances (US-ALRT-008 NFR). A serialisation test asserts the payload against an allow-list of fields.
- **Retry and failure**: exponential backoff up to the outbox `max_attempts`; persistent failure **disables the webhook** and raises a notification about it (US-ALRT-008 scenario 3) while leaving the in-app record intact.
- URL and secret entry in SCR-091 behind the same flag, write-only (never read back), with the acknowledgement dialog for a public endpoint.

## Out of scope
Inbound webhooks (receiving signals from outside) — not a planned capability. Any webhook that triggers an action; alerts never act. Third-party integrations (Slack/Discord formatting) — the payload is generic JSON.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A Tailscale endpoint receives a signed payload
  Given a configured endpoint on the Tailscale network
  When the alert fires
  Then a JSON payload is POSTed with a valid HMAC-SHA256 signature and timestamp headers, and the receiver can verify it with the per-alert secret
Scenario: A public endpoint is refused by default (failure)
  Given a public internet URL
  When the alert is saved
  Then it is refused with an explanation, unless the owner has explicitly allow-listed it and acknowledged the warning
Scenario: SSRF targets are blocked (failure)
  When the URL resolves to loopback, link-local, a cloud metadata address, or an RFC1918 address outside the Tailscale CIDR, or the endpoint issues a redirect
  Then the request is refused before any connection is made and the refusal is audited
Scenario: DNS rebinding cannot succeed (edge)
  Given a hostname that resolves to an allowed address and then to a blocked one
  Then the connection uses the pinned resolved address and the second resolution cannot change the target
Scenario: Persistent failure disables the webhook loudly (failure)
  Given the endpoint returns 500 on every attempt
  Then delivery retries with backoff to the limit, the webhook channel is disabled, a notification explains why, and the in-app alert record is untouched
Scenario: No secret ever leaves (failure)
  When the serialised payload for every alert type is inspected
  Then it contains no API key, no account credential, no balance and no webhook secret
```

## Technical notes / design
Implement egress through a single hardened HTTP client used only by this adapter, with a connector that takes a pre-resolved IP plus a Host header. Redirect following is disabled at the client level, not by inspecting responses. The allow-list is stored in configuration (not per-alert), so adding a public endpoint is an owner-level act recorded in the audit log.

Secret handling reuses the E27 credential broker (envelope encryption, KEK outside the application DB); the API never returns `webhook_url` or the secret, and `GET /alerts` omits both columns by the E40-T01 read allow-list.

## Test plan
- Unit: URL policy matrix (loopback, link-local, metadata IPs, RFC1918 in/out of the Tailscale CIDR, https/http, redirect, userinfo-in-URL, IPv6 forms, decimal/octal IP encodings); HMAC construction and verification; payload field allow-list; backoff schedule; disable-on-persistent-failure.
- Integration: against a local test receiver verifying signatures; a rebinding-simulation test with a mutating resolver.
- Security: the abuse cases from E40-X01 run as required checks; DAST (ZAP) pass over the alert configuration endpoints.
- Coverage ≥90% on the egress policy module (security-critical).

## Security notes
This is the highest-risk ticket in E40. Threats: **SSRF** (the primary one — reaching the Tailscale control plane, the host's own admin surfaces, or a cloud metadata endpoint), **secret exfiltration** via a crafted message template, **amplification** (an alert configured to fire constantly at a third-party endpoint), **replay** of a captured payload, and **credential exposure** of the webhook secret. Controls as scoped above. Data classification: `webhook_url_enc`/`webhook_secret_enc` are SECRET. This story **requires** a security review sign-off (E40-X01) and must not be enabled in any environment before the E43 pen-test has covered it.

## Accessibility notes
The URL/secret fields and the public-endpoint acknowledgement dialog follow the standard form and `role="alertdialog"` patterns; the acknowledgement must be text, not an icon, and must state the specific risk.

## Performance notes
Webhook delivery is asynchronous through the outbox and must never block in-app delivery: a slow endpoint may not delay the toast. Per-endpoint concurrency cap 2, request timeout 5 s, total attempt budget bounded by the outbox `max_attempts`.

## Observability
`cv_alert_webhook_total{outcome}`, `cv_alert_webhook_latency_seconds`, `cv_alert_webhook_blocked_total{reason}` (the SSRF-policy counter — any non-zero value is worth investigating), `cv_alert_webhook_disabled_total`. Audit: `alert.webhook_configured`, `alert.webhook_allowlisted`, `alert.webhook_disabled`, `alert.webhook_blocked`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Egress policy implemented with ≥90% coverage and the full URL policy matrix green as a required check.
- [ ] HMAC signing verified against an independent receiver implementation.
- [ ] Payload allow-list test green; no secret present in any serialisation.
- [ ] Security engineer review and sign-off; DAST pass; included in the E43 pen-test scope.
- [ ] Flag `alerts.webhook_enabled` default off everywhere; enablement recorded as an R5 decision.
- [ ] Docs: `22-api-openapi.yaml` and the runbook updated; changelog fragment.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E40-T04` (dispatcher and channel adapter interface), `E40-X01` (abuse cases and SSRF controls must exist before the egress path is written), `E27-T02` (credential broker for the secret), `E43`/`E44` gate its enablement.

## Branch

## Context
Everything else in E40 sits on two tables that are already fully specified in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.5 and listed in the migration register as `0009_alerts` (§ migrations table: `alerts`, `alert_deliveries`, `outbox`). - `outbox` topics registered for E40: `alert.deliver` and `webhook.post` (the table itself already exists from §3.10.4; this task only registers the topic constants and their `dedup_key` construction rules).

The compiler and API (E40-T02), the evaluator (E40-T03), the dispatcher (E40-T04). The `rules` tables (E35-T02). Column-level encryption of `webhook_url_enc`/`webhook_secret_enc` — the columns are created here but only written by E40-S03 via the E27 credential broker.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Migration matches the specification exactly

  Then there is no difference in columns, types, defaults, constraints, indexes or triggers
Scenario: Delivery history cannot be deleted by the application role
  Given a delivery row and a session as the application role
  When a DELETE is attempted
  Then the trg_ad_append trigger raises and the row survives
Scenario: The retention job can still purge (edge)
  Given the retention job connected as cv_owner
  When it purges deliveries older than the retained window
  Then the deletes succeed because the trigger exempts session_user = cv_owner
Scenario: Constraints reject bad data (failure)
  When an alert is inserted with cooldown_seconds = 90000, or with six channels, or with channel 'webhook' and a NULL webhook_url_enc
  Then each insert fails on al_cooldown, al_channels and al_webhook respectively
```

`dedup_key` construction — `alert.deliver`: `f"{delivery_id}"` (one outbox row per delivery row, so replay is naturally idempotent). `webhook.post`: `f"{alert_id}:{fired_at_ms}:{attempt_group}"`. title: Implement the notify-only alert compiler and the alert CRUD API
body:
## Context
`AlertConditionIr` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` is the condition half of the rule IR with `actions` deliberately omitted, and the endpoint description states the invariant plainly: *"an alert can never place an order regardless of what the user authors"*. That invariant is enforced here, at the compiler and the write API, and nowhere else can it be weakened. This is the security-critical task of E40.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `apps/api/cv/alerts/compiler.py` — `AlertCompiler` wrapping E35's IR validator:
  1. schema-validate against `AlertConditionIr` with `additionalProperties: false` (so an `actions` key is a schema error, not a silently ignored field);
  2. structurally reject any action-bearing node anywhere in the tree, including inside `variables`, using an allow-list of permitted node kinds rather than a deny-list of forbidden ones;
  3. resolve every referenced metric against E35's `MetricRegistry`, rejecting unknown metrics with the offending `node_id`;
  4. validate the trigger (`RuleTrigger`): `on_bar_close` requires `timeframe`, `on_timer` requires `interval_ms ≥ 100`, `on_schedule` requires a 5-field UTC cron, `on_metric_change` requires `metric`;
  5. canonicalise and compute `condition_hash` (sha256 over the canonical form) reusing E35's canonicalisation so an identical condition authored in a rule and in an alert hashes identically;
  6. flag conditions referencing **estimated** detector metrics so the UI can render the "(estimated)" qualifier (US-ALRT-003 scenario 2).
- `message_template` validation: Mustache-style placeholders resolved against an **allow-listed** variable namespace derived from the compiled condition's context (`market.*`, `footprint.*`, `position.*`, `alert.*`); any placeholder outside the allow-list is a 422, and no placeholder may resolve to a secret-bearing field.
- REST surface in `apps/api/cv/alerts/router.py`, exactly as specified:
  - `GET /api/v1/alerts` (cursor, limit, `enabled`, `symbol` filters) → `Page<Alert>`;
  - `POST /api/v1/alerts` (`AlertInput`, `Idempotency-Key` recommended) → 201 `Alert`, 422 `RuleIrInvalid`;
  - `GET /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}` → `Alert`, 404;
  - `PUT /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}` (`If-Match`) → 200 or 412 `PreconditionFailed`;
  - `DELETE /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}` → 204 (soft delete, freeing the unique name);
  - `PUT /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}/enabled` → 200 `Alert`.
- RBAC: `alerts:read` / `alerts:write`, `scope: self` — a user may only ever see and mutate their own alerts; enforced in a dependency, not per-handler.
- Audit events on every mutation: `alerts.create`, `alert.updated`, `alert.enabled_changed`, `alert.deleted` (an alert is audited because it can participate in a notification chain).
- Contract tests generated from the OpenAPI document.

## Out of scope
Evaluation (E40-T03), delivery (E40-T04), deliveries/notifications endpoints (E40-T04), webhook URL storage (E40-S03), the editor UI (E40-S01).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A valid price alert compiles and persists
  When POST /api/v1/alerts is called with the priceCross example from 22-api-openapi.yaml
  Then 201 is returned, condition_hash is populated, the alert is enabled, and alerts.create is audited
Scenario: An action-bearing payload is rejected (failure)
  When condition_ir carries an actions key, or an action node nested inside variables, or an operand naming a rule action
  Then 422 RuleIrInvalid is returned naming the offending node_id, nothing is persisted, and no OMS interface is touched
Scenario: Unknown metric is refused with a usable message (failure)
  When a condition references a metric absent from the E35 registry
  Then 422 names the metric and the node_id, and lists the nearest valid metric names
Scenario: Concurrent edits do not silently overwrite (edge)
  Given two clients hold the same ETag
  When both PUT the alert
  Then the second receives 412 PreconditionFailed and its payload is not applied
Scenario: Cross-user access is impossible (failure)
  Given user B's alert id
  When user A calls GET, PUT, DELETE or PUT /enabled on it
  Then each returns 404 (not 403, so existence is not disclosed), no state changes, and the denial is audited
Scenario: A template cannot exfiltrate a secret (failure)
  When message_template references a placeholder outside the allow-listed namespace
  Then 422 is returned naming the placeholder
```

## Technical notes / design
The allow-list approach in step 2 is deliberate: a deny-list of action node kinds fails open the moment E35 adds a node kind. The permitted set is `{condition, comparison, logical, operand:metric, operand:const, operand:variable, trigger}`; anything else is rejected by construction, and a unit test enumerates E35's full node-kind registry and asserts every kind is either in the allow-list or rejected — so adding a node kind in E35 without considering alerts fails E40's tests rather than silently widening the surface.

`condition_hash` reuses E35's canonicalisation (ADR-0025-rule-ir-canonicalisation) because E40-T03 keys shared metric subscriptions on it; a private canonicalisation would silently defeat the sharing.

Error code for IR problems is the shared `RuleIrInvalid` 422 response, so the alert editor can reuse the rule editor's ValidationPanel rendering unchanged.

## Test plan
- Unit: compiler accept/reject matrix incl. the node-kind enumeration test; trigger validation per trigger type; template allow-list; canonical hash equality against an equivalent E35 rule condition; estimated-metric flagging.
- Property: fuzz IR trees (hypothesis) asserting no tree containing an action node ever compiles.
- Contract: every operation and every documented response code against the OpenAPI document.
- Integration: full CRUD lifecycle incl. soft-delete freeing the unique name and re-creation with the same name.
- Security: the cross-user matrix from the AC, run as a required check.
- Coverage ≥90% on `cv.alerts.compiler` (security-relevant module, local policy above the 85% floor).

## Security notes
Threats from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: **Elevation of privilege** — an alert that can act becomes an unaudited order path; mitigated by the allow-list compiler plus the fuzz property test. **Information disclosure** — cross-user alert reads; mitigated by `scope: self` enforced in a dependency and the 404-not-403 policy. **Tampering** — last-writer-wins edits; mitigated by `If-Match`. **Injection** — template placeholders; mitigated by the namespace allow-list. Data classification: alert definitions are Internal; `webhook_url_enc`/`webhook_secret_enc` are SECRET and are not writable through this task's endpoints. Security review label required — reviewed under E40-X01.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — API. The 422 payload shape (node_id + human message + suggestions) is what makes the editor's accessible ValidationPanel possible, so the message text must be plain language, not a schema dump.

## Performance notes
Compile + validate must complete in ≤300 ms p95 to meet the SCR-091 round-trip budget, including the metric-registry lookup (registry is cached in-process, invalidated on E35's vocabulary-version bump). `GET /alerts` is cursor-paginated and must use `ux_alerts_name`/`ix_alerts_live`; assert no sequential scan at 10k alerts.

## Observability
Metrics `cv_alert_compile_seconds`, `cv_alert_compile_rejected_total{reason}` (`action_node`, `unknown_metric`, `bad_trigger`, `bad_template`), `cv_alerts_total{enabled}`. Structured log on every rejection with `node_id` and `reason`, no payload echo. Audit events as listed above.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Compiler, router and RBAC dependency implemented; OpenAPI document matches the implementation (contract tests green).
- [ ] Node-kind enumeration test and IR fuzz property test in CI as required checks.
- [ ] Coverage ≥90% on the compiler; ≥85% on the module.

title: Build the server-side alert evaluator with gating and storm suppression
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** the gating, storm-suppression and snooze lifecycle (armed→…→firing→resolved) is built directly on the library via the factory; per-tick condition evaluation itself stays plain code (BENCH-2: 381 ev/s vs a 2000 ev/s target, hot-path exclusion, 29 §3).

This is module **M22**'s heart: the component that turns armed alert rows into firings. It must evaluate server-side (alerts fire with the client closed), share the E35 metric bus without duplicating evaluation, and never let a storm of detector events make the product unusable. The placement decision (shared vs separate evaluator) comes from E40-K01's ADR-0019; this task implements whichever it chose.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implement the `B10` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B10.alert.machine.json` (committed by E50-S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('alert', lane=…)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/b10_alert.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_b10_alert.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.
- `apps/api/cv/alerts/evaluator.py` — `AlertEvaluator`:
  - **Warm-up**: load all rows where `enabled AND deleted_at IS NULL` (index `ix_alerts_live`), group by `condition_hash`, and create **one** metric subscription per distinct hash, fanned out to the alert rows sharing it.
  - **Live reconfiguration**: react to create/update/delete/enable/snooze without a restart, via the same in-process event the API emits; a changed condition re-keys its subscription and drops the old one when its last referent leaves.
  - **Gating pipeline**, evaluated in this exact order on every candidate fire: `enabled` → not soft-deleted → `expires_at` not passed → `snoozed_until` not in the future → symbol/category mute (E40-S02 preferences) unless the alert is on the critical-override list → `trigger_mode` → `cooldown_seconds` → storm suppressor → dispatch.
  - **Trigger modes**: `once` — fire, then set `enabled = false` atomically with the firing so a concurrent tick cannot double-fire; `every_time` — fire subject to `cooldown_seconds`; `once_per_bar` — fire at most once per bar keyed on `(alert_id, timeframe, bar_open_ms)`, with late-tick bar revisions not re-opening the key.
  - **Expiry semantics**: alerts do **not** expire on a timer (US-ALRT-001 scenario 3) — only an explicit `expires_at` disarms one, and when it does, the alert moves to the Triggered/Expired presentation rather than vanishing.
  - **Auto-disarm on source loss** (US-ALRT-002 scenario 2): when a referenced metric's data source becomes unavailable (E35 registry emits source-degraded), the alert is disarmed and a delivery is raised **stating why**, never failing silently.
  - **Storm suppressor**: per-user sliding window using the threshold and window ratified in E40-D01 and validated in E40-K01 (default `>20 deliveries / 60 s`); excess firings are still **recorded individually** in `alert_deliveries` with `status = 'suppressed'` and are aggregated into one summary delivery ("18 further alerts fired for BTCUSDT and 2 others"), so nothing is lost from history.
  - **Firing transaction**: the `alert_deliveries` row(s), the `outbox` row(s), and the `last_fired_at` / `fire_count` / `enabled` updates commit in one transaction — a crash between "decide" and "send" can neither lose nor duplicate (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.10.4).
  - **Evaluation snapshot**: the values that fired the alert are written to `alert_deliveries.context` so the alert history carries "the firing evaluation attached" (roadmap §7.2) and SCR-092's detail drawer has something to render.
- Startup/shutdown integration with the app lifespan; graceful drain so an in-flight firing completes or rolls back whole.

## Out of scope
Channel transport and the dispatcher poller (E40-T04). REST/WS surfaces for deliveries (E40-T04). Any UI. Webhook egress (E40-S03). Rule *actions* — alerts have none.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A price alert fires with no client connected
  Given an armed crossing alert at 65000 on BTCUSDT and zero WS clients
  When the recorded feed crosses 65000
  Then an alert_deliveries row is committed within 1 s with the crossing values in context

  Given a one-shot alert and two ticks satisfying it in the same millisecond
  Then exactly one delivery is created and the alert ends disabled
Scenario: Recurring alerts respect the cooldown
  Given an every_time alert with cooldown_seconds = 60 and a condition true continuously
  Then it fires at most once per 60 s, and the re-arm is visible in the alert row
Scenario: Bar-close semantics are honoured (edge)
  Given a once_per_bar alert on 5m and a late tick that revises the current bar
  Then the alert does not fire a second time for that bar
Scenario: A storm aggregates without losing history (edge)
  Given 25 qualifying firings for one user inside 60 s
  Then the first N are delivered normally, the remainder are recorded with status suppressed, one summary delivery is produced, and the alert centre can show all 25
Scenario: A dead metric source disarms loudly (failure)
  Given an alert on a metric whose source goes unavailable
  Then the alert is disarmed and a delivery explains why, rather than the alert silently never firing again
Scenario: A crash mid-fire loses nothing (failure)
  Given the process is killed between the delivery insert and the poller run
  Then on restart the outbox row is still pending and is delivered exactly once
```

## Technical notes / design

**Statechart contract.** Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B10.1–.8. Mandatory config: `29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §1.2 (`79-r14-final-readiness-verdict.md` §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in `29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §3 stay plain code.
Subscription sharing is keyed on `condition_hash` — the same hash E40-T02 computes with E35's canonicalisation, which is why both must use one canonicaliser.

Cooldown and `once_per_bar` keys live in an in-process TTL map backed by `alerts.last_fired_at` so a restart cannot reopen a cooldown window; on warm-up the map is rebuilt from the table.

`once` disarm uses a conditional update (`UPDATE alerts SET enabled = false WHERE id = :id AND enabled`) inside the firing transaction; zero rows affected means another worker won the race and this evaluation discards its firing.

The storm suppressor is per **user**, not per alert, because the user-visible failure is "too many notifications", which no per-alert limit can bound.

Critical-override entries (from E40-D01's ratified list: daily-loss breach, liquidation proximity, connection loss, kill-switch engagement, fan-out partial failure) bypass mute and quiet hours but **not** the crash-safety or recording path.

## Test plan

**Statechart test plan additions:**
- Pure-API unit tests of the `b10_alert` binding module using a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership in `tests/xstate_contract/test_b10_alert.py`, covering both spellings and every §B10.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist→restore) at every quiescence point this ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a `machine_hash` or HMAC mismatch.
- Unit: each gate in isolation; the gating order (a test asserts snooze is checked before cooldown so a snoozed alert does not consume its cooldown); trigger-mode state machines; `once_per_bar` key derivation for every supported timeframe incl. late revision; storm-suppressor window arithmetic at boundaries (exactly N, N+1).
- Integration: recorded Bybit fixture replay asserting an exact expected firing sequence (deterministic — same window, same sequence across runs); auto-disarm on simulated source loss; subscription count equals distinct condition hashes for a 100-alert/12-condition corpus.
- Chaos: process kill between insert and dispatch (covered end-to-end in E40-Q02).
- Perf: 500 armed alerts / 20 symbols under a recorded high-rate window, asserting p95 condition→record ≤1 s (E40-Q02 owns the gate; this task ships the benchmark).
- Coverage ≥85% on `cv.alerts.evaluator`.

## Security notes
**Denial of service** is the headline threat and it is self-inflicted: an unbounded alert count or an unthrottled detector stream can starve evaluation. Controls — a per-user armed-alert cap (configurable, default 200) enforced at `POST /alerts`, the storm suppressor, and a bounded evaluation queue that sheds with a counted metric rather than growing without limit. **Tampering**: the evaluator writes history that is append-only by trigger. **Repudiation**: every firing carries its evaluation snapshot, so "why did this fire" is answerable from data.

## Performance notes

title: Build the delivery dispatcher, deliveries API and the alerts WS topic
body:
## Context
US-ALRT-005's NFR is the design constraint: *"no channel may be the single source of truth — the alert centre always records everything."* This task builds the fan-out from a recorded firing to the channels, the read surfaces the UI consumes, and the live `alerts` WS topic, all on top of the transactional outbox so a channel failure degrades delivery without losing the record.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `apps/api/cv/alerts/dispatcher.py` — outbox poller for topic `alert.deliver`:
  - one `alert_deliveries` row **per channel per firing**, so a failed email and a delivered toast are separately visible;
  - channel adapters: `in_app` (always succeeds — it is the record itself, immediately visible over WS), `desktop` (delivered to the Electron shell over the existing WS as a client-side instruction; the shell's OS-permission state is reported back and surfaced as the SCR-090 delivery-failure chip), `email` (via the configured relay from E04; retried per policy), `webhook` and `push` adapters **registered but disabled** — `webhook` lands in E40-S03 (R5), `push` is not in scope (Android is out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14) and is rejected at the API with a clear message;
  - retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, `max_attempts` from the outbox row (default 8), `attempt` mirrored onto `alert_deliveries.attempt`, terminal failure sets `status = 'failed'` with `error_message` and, for the failing channel only, raises a notification about the channel failure — the underlying alert record is untouched;
  - status transitions `queued → sent | failed | suppressed`, and `sent → acked` on user ack; DELETE is impossible by trigger.
- REST surface:
  - `GET /api/v1/alerts/deliveries` (cursor, limit, `status`, `alert_id`, `unacked_only`, `from`, `to`) → `Page<AlertDelivery>`;
  - `POST /api/v1/alerts/deliveries/{deliveryId}/ack` → `AlertDelivery`;
  - `POST /api/v1/alerts/deliveries/ack-all` → `{acknowledged: int}`;
  - `GET /api/v1/notifications` — the unified read-model union over `alert_deliveries`, `rule_events`, `order_events` and `system_events`, filtered to what the caller may see, with `kind` (`alert|rule|order|risk|system`) and `unread_only` filters; this is the scroll-back behind SCR-014.
- WS topic `alerts` per `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`: payload `AlertUpdate` (`deliveries[]` + `unacked_count`), subscription option `unacked_only`, cadence **250 ms**, permission `alerts:read`, scope "own alerts only", snapshot-on-subscribe then deltas, resync on gap per the standard envelope.
- Backpressure: the `alerts` topic coalesces within its 250 ms window and never grows an unbounded per-connection queue; overflow drops to a "resync required" marker rather than silently truncating.

## Out of scope
Evaluation (E40-T03). Webhook egress and its SSRF controls (E40-S03). Any UI (E40-S01..S04). Email relay provisioning (E04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A firing reaches every configured channel
  Given an alert with channels [in_app, desktop]
  When it fires
  Then two alert_deliveries rows are created, the in_app row is visible over the alerts WS topic within 250 ms, and the desktop row transitions to sent when the shell confirms
Scenario: A failing channel does not erase the record
  Given email delivery returns 500 on every attempt
  Then the email delivery ends failed with its error recorded, the in-app record still exists and is unaffected, and a channel-failure notification is raised once, not per attempt
Scenario: Acknowledgement is idempotent (edge)
  When the same delivery is acked twice
  Then the second call returns the same acked state and does not change acked_at
Scenario: Exactly-once under restart (failure)
  Given the process restarts with pending outbox rows
  Then each pending row is delivered exactly once, proven by the unique (topic, dedup_key) index and a duplicate-delivery assertion
Scenario: A user cannot read another user's deliveries (failure)
  Given user B's deliveryId
  When user A acks it or lists with alert_id belonging to B
  Then 404 is returned, nothing changes, and the denial is audited
Scenario: Push is refused clearly (edge)
  When an alert is created with channel push
  Then the API returns 422 explaining push is not available in this deployment, rather than accepting an alert that can never deliver
```

## Technical notes / design
The poller leases rows with `locked_by`/`locked_until` and a `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` claim so multiple workers are safe. Idempotency on the consumer side comes from the delivery row itself: a channel adapter is only invoked for a row in `queued`, and the transition to `sent` is a conditional update.

`GET /notifications` is a read-model union, not a table: implement it as a UNION ALL over four sources with a shared `(ts, id)` keyset cursor, each source pre-filtered by the caller's scope. It is read-only and has no permissions of its own (`x-rbac: { permissions: [], scope: self }`) — visibility comes from the per-source filters.

Desktop notifications are not a server-side transport: the server marks the delivery `queued` for the `desktop` channel, the Electron shell renders the OS notification on receipt over WS and posts back the outcome, which is what lets SCR-090 show "Desktop notification blocked by the OS".

## Test plan
- Unit: retry/backoff schedule; status transition legality (an illegal transition raises); per-channel row creation; ack idempotency; union cursor ordering across sources with identical timestamps.
- Contract: all four REST operations and the `alerts` WS schema against `23-ws-protocol.md` §15.7 — a schema-diff test fails if the payload drifts.
- Integration: end-to-end fire → deliver → WS push → ack, with a fault-injected failing channel; restart-with-pending-outbox exactly-once test.
- Perf: WS cadence held at 250 ms under a firing burst; `GET /notifications` p95 <200 ms at 1M rows across the four sources.
- Coverage ≥85% on `cv.alerts.dispatcher` and the router.

## Security notes
**Spoofing/authorisation**: deliveries are `scope: self`; the ack endpoints must resolve ownership from the delivery's `user_id`, never from a client-supplied user id. **Information disclosure**: `GET /notifications` unions four sources with different scoping rules — the union must apply each source's own filter, and a test asserts a viewer-role user sees no order events they lack `orders:read` for. **DoS**: `ack-all` must be bounded (batched update with a cap and a continuation), not an unbounded statement. **Repudiation**: delivery history is append-only. No secret ever enters a delivery title/body/context — asserted by a test that scans serialised payloads for the SECRET column names.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — API/WS. The `unacked_count` field exists so the UI can render an accurate accessible name ("Notifications, 3 unread") without counting client-side.

## Performance notes
`alerts` topic cadence 250 ms with coalescing; unacked-count query hits `ix_ad_user_unack`; the deliveries list is cursor-paginated (never OFFSET); `GET /notifications` is the scroll-back for a 500-row virtualised client list, so it must support a page size of 500 without degradation.

## Observability
`cv_alert_delivery_total{channel,status}`, `cv_alert_delivery_latency_seconds{channel}` (firing → sent), `cv_alert_delivery_attempts` (histogram), `cv_outbox_depth{topic}`, `cv_outbox_dead_total{topic}`, `cv_ws_alerts_subscribers`. Alertmanager rule (E04): `cv_outbox_depth{topic="alert.deliver"}` sustained >100 for 5 min → warn; any `cv_outbox_dead_total` increase → warn.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Dispatcher, four REST operations and the `alerts` WS topic implemented and contract-tested.
- [ ] Exactly-once-under-restart test green in CI.
- [ ] Push rejected explicitly; webhook adapter registered but disabled with a feature flag `alerts.webhook_enabled = false`.
- [ ] Metrics exported, Alertmanager rules added.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85%; `22-api-openapi.yaml` and `23-ws-protocol.md` reconciled.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

`E40-T03` produces the firings this task delivers. `E04` supplies the email relay and the metrics/Alertmanager plumbing. `E09` supplies session scope and permissions.
